      """Event colors as a trait-like policy, portable across providers.
      
      Munazzim colors prayers fixed and cycles everything else (TUI-only there).
      dir3 ports the *idea* to real calendar colors: a :class:`ColorPolicy` decides
      *which* color family an event gets (as a neutral slot ``0..10``), each
      provider renders the slot its own way (GCal: ``colorId`` ``"1".."11"``).
      
      Rules (munazzim-inspired): the default policy keeps prayers yellow; the
      optional status policy colors prayers at the Adhan green, shifted prayers
      yellow, prayers that take lecture time orange, and critical prayers red.
      Every other event gets a deterministic color from its name - same name, same
      color.
      
      Implement the trait for custom behavior - any object with
      ``color_for(name, index) -> int | None`` works, no inheritance needed::
      
          class MyColors:
              def color_for(self, name, index):
                  return 10 if "sleep" in name.lower() else None
      """
      from __future__ import annotations
      
      from dataclasses import dataclass, field
      from typing import Protocol, runtime_checkable
      
      
      @runtime_checkable
      class ColorPolicy(Protocol):
          """Trait: maps an event to a color slot ``0..10``, or ``None`` for default."""
      
          def color_for(self, name: str, index: int) -> int | None:
              """Slot for the event with this name at this (per-day) position."""
              ...  # pragma: no cover - trait
      
      
      #: Slot -> GCal ``colorId``. Hand-picked so prayers read naturally
      #: (dawn grape, midday banana, sunset tomato, night blueberry).
      PALETTE = ("3", "6", "5", "7", "11", "9", "1", "2", "4", "8", "10")
      
      #: Normalized prayer names - always rendered yellow (GCal Banana).
      # lange Gebetsnamen -> kurze, informative Varianten für die Anzeige
      SHORT_PRAYER_NAMES: dict[str, str] = {
          "fajr": "Fajr",
          "sunrise": "Sonnenaufgang",
          "dhuhr": "Dhuhr",
          "duhr": "Dhuhr",
          "jumuah": "Jumuah",
          "asr": "Asr",
          "maghrib": "Maghrib",
          "isha": "Isha",
          "sunset": "Sonnenuntergang",
      }
      
      PRAYER_NAMES = frozenset(
          {"fajr", "sunrise", "dhuhr", "duhr", "jumuah", "asr", "maghrib", "isha"}
      )
      
      #: Slot rendering as yellow (GCal Banana ``"5"``) on every provider.
      YELLOW_SLOT = 2
      
      #: Slot rendering as green (GCal Sage ``"2"``) on every provider.
      GREEN_SLOT = 7
      
      #: Slot rendering as red (GCal Tomato ``"11"``) on every provider.
      RED_SLOT = 4
      
      #: Slot rendering as orange (GCal Tangerine ``"6"``) on every provider.
      ORANGE_SLOT = 1
      
      #: Markers a plan can put into a prayer name to describe its schedule state.
      SHIFTED_MARKER = "verschoben"
      CRITICAL_MARKER = "kritisch"
      KERAHAT_MARKER = "kerahat"
      ORANGE_MARKER = "von der vorlesung"
      
      
      def shorten_event_name(name: str | None) -> str:
          """Kürzt lange Event-Namen, ohne Information zu verlieren.
      
          Entfernt:
          - überflüssige Beschreibungen in Klammern, wenn der Kontext klar ist
          - wiederholte Präfixe wie "Weg: " wenn bereits am Anfang
          - redundante Zusätze wie "(Moschee, nur Fardh)" → "(Moschee)"
          - Indexnummern bei Vorlesungen, wenn sie länger als nötig sind
          - verbose Reiseroute-Beschreibungen zu "Weg: A >> B"
      
          Behält aber alle wichtigen Informationen bei: Adhan-Zeiten, Verschiebungen,
          Kerahat-Status, Vorlesungs-Überschneidungen, Fardh/Hadith-Info etc.
          """
          if not name:
              return ""
      
          text = str(name)
          normalized = normalize_event_name(text)
          head, sep, rest = normalized.partition(" ")
      
          # LANGE Vorlesungsnamen kürzen: "EN 732 ROBS (Uebung, Marvin)" → "EN732 ROBS (Ü)"
          if head and (rest.startswith("(") or any(k in rest for k in ("uebung", "übung", "exercise", "exercises", "lab", "labs", "lecture", "lectures", "seminar", "vorlesung"))):
              import re
      
              # Kursnummer + Name + Klammerinfo kompaktieren
              match = re.match(r"^([a-z]+)\s+(\d+)\s+([a-z0-9]+)\s+\(([^)]+)\)$", text, re.IGNORECASE)
              if match:
                  prefix, nummer, name_kurz, info = match.groups()
                  info_lower = info.lower()
                  if "uebung" in info_lower or "übung" in info_lower:
                      info = "Ü"
                  elif "exercise" in info_lower or "exercises" in info_lower:
                      info = "Ex"
                  elif "lab" in info_lower or "labs" in info_lower:
                      info = "Lab"
                  elif "lecture" in info_lower or "lectures" in info_lower:
                      info = "V"
                  elif "seminar" in info_lower:
                      info = "S"
                  elif "vorlesung" in info_lower:
                      info = "V"
                  return f"{prefix}{nummer} {name_kurz} ({info})".strip()
      
          # Weg-Namen kompaktieren: "Weg: Mertensstr. >> Berlin, Galenstr. BUS 136" → "Weg: Mertensstr. >> Berlin"
          if head == "weg" and ">>" in text:
              import re
      
              match = re.match(r"^Weg:\s*(.+?)\s*>>\s*(.+?),?\s*(?:[A-Z]{2,4}\s*\d+)?\s*(?:BUS\s*\d+)?\s*$", text, re.IGNORECASE)
              if match:
                  von = match.group(1).strip()
                  nach = match.group(2).strip()
                  return f"Weg: {von} >> {nach}"
      
          # Redundante Klammer-Inhalte entfernen
          if rest.startswith("("):
              import re
      
              text = re.sub(
                  r"\((\s*)(Moschee|NahMoschee|allein)(,\s*(nur Fardh|nur Hadith|Fardh|Hadith))?(\s*)\)",
                  lambda m: f"({'Moschee' if 'moschee' in m.group(1).lower() or 'nahmoschee' in m.group(1).lower() else 'allein'})",
                  text,
                  flags=re.IGNORECASE,
              )
      
          return text
      
      
      def event_summary(name: str | None, icon_policy: object | None = None, index: int = 0) -> str:
          """Event-Name mit Icon und gekürztem Text für die Anzeige.
      
          Kombiniert:
          - :func:`shorten_event_name` für die Namensverkürzung
          - :meth:`icon_policy.icon_for` für das Icon (wenn vorhanden)
          
          Rückgabe: ``"🕋 Fajr"`` oder ``"🏫 EN732 ROBS (Ü)"`` etc.
          """
          if not name:
              return ""
      
          short = shorten_event_name(name)
          icon = ""
          if icon_policy is not None:
              icon_fn = getattr(icon_policy, "icon_for", None)
              if callable(icon_fn):
                  icon = icon_fn(name, index) or ""
      
          if icon:
              return f"{icon} {short}"
          return short
      
      
      def normalize_event_name(name: object) -> str:
          return str(name or "").strip().casefold()
      
      
      def name_slot(name: object) -> int:
          """Deterministic color slot from the event name.
      
          The name's bytes are summed as numbers, modulo the palette length -
          so the same name always yields the same slot on every provider::
      
              sum(b"coding") % 11 == 1
          """
          total = sum(normalize_event_name(name).encode("utf-8"))
          return total % len(PALETTE)
      
      
      def to_gcal_color_id(slot: object) -> str | None:
          """Render a policy slot as a GCal ``colorId`` (``None`` = calendar default)."""
          try:
              index = int(slot)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
          except (TypeError, ValueError):
              return None
          if isinstance(slot, bool) or not 0 <= index <= 10:
              return None
          return PALETTE[index]
      
      
      def _slot_from_color_id(value: object) -> int | None:
          """User-facing GCal ``colorId`` (``1``..``11``) -> palette slot (round-trip safe)."""
          if isinstance(value, bool):
              return None
          try:
              text = str(int(str(value).strip()))
          except (TypeError, ValueError):
              return None
          try:
              return PALETTE.index(text)
          except ValueError:
              return None
      
      
      @dataclass
      class PrayerColorPolicy:
          """Default trait impl: prayers yellow, everything else name-hashed."""
      
          def color_for(self, name: str, index: int) -> int | None:
              if normalize_event_name(name) in PRAYER_NAMES:
                  return YELLOW_SLOT
              return name_slot(name)
      
      
      class IconPolicy:
          """Trait: attaches one unicode marker to an event summary.
      
          Markers are orthogonal to colors: :class:`ColorPolicy` picks the
          calendar fill, :class:`IconPolicy` picks the inline glyph that
          readable output and calendar titles carry around.
      
          dir3 bundles a :class:`DefaultIconPolicy` that tags prayers with 🕋,
          lectures/Übungen with 🏫, and travel with 🛣.  Implement the trait
          yourself when you want different icons - any object with
          ``icon_for(name, index) -> str`` works, no inheritance needed::
      
              class MyIcons:
                  def icon_for(self, name, index):
                      return '  📚 ' if 'lecture' in name.lower() else ''
          """
      
          def icon_for(self, name: str, index: int) -> str:
              """Icon marker to prefix an event summary with."""
              ...  # pragma: no cover - trait
      
      
      @dataclass
      class DefaultIconPolicy:
          """Bundled icon policy: 🕋 prayers, 🏫 lectures/Übungen, 🛣 travel.
      
          ``index`` is the per-day position of the event - it lets the policy
          decide differently for the same name in different places if ever
          needed, though the default policy is name-driven.
          """
      
          _icons: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
      
          def __post_init__(self) -> None:
              self._icons.update(
                  **{
                      "": "🕋",  # bare prayer name
                      "fajr": "🕋",
                      "sunrise": "🕋",
                      "dhuhr": "🕋",
                      "duhr": "🕋",
                      "jumuah": "🕋",
                      "asr": "🕋",
                      "maghrib": "🕋",
                      "isha": "🕋",
                  }
              )
      
          def icon_for(self, name: str, index: int) -> str:
              normalized = normalize_event_name(name)
              head, _, rest = normalized.partition(" ")
      
              # bare prayer name (and plain parenthetical variants) → 🕋
              if head in PRAYER_NAMES or (head in PRAYER_NAMES and rest.startswith("(")):
                  return self._icons.get(head, "🕋")
      
              # lectures / Übungen / exercises / labs → 🏫
              if self._looks_like_lecture(rest if head else normalized):
                  return "🏫"
              if self._looks_like_lecture(head):
                  return "🏫"
      
              # travel / journey / way / trip → 🛣
              if self._looks_like_travel(normalized):
                  return "🛣"
      
              return ""
      
          @staticmethod
          def _looks_like_lecture(rest: str) -> bool:
              text = rest.strip().lower()
              if not text:
                  return False
              if text.startswith("("):
                  text = text.strip("() ")
              return any(k in text for k in ("übung", "uebung", "exercise", "exercises", "lab", "labs", "lecture", "lectures", "seminar", "vorlesung"))
      
          @staticmethod
          def _looks_like_travel(name: str) -> bool:
              lowered = name.lower()
              stripped = lowered.strip().strip("() ")
              if any(w in stripped for w in ("weg", "travel", "trip", "journey", "fahrt", "commute", "zurück", "zurueck", "hin", "weg:", "->", ">>")):
                  return True
              return False
      
      
      _CHAIN_ORDER_KEY = "__dir3_icon_chain__"
      
      
      def icon_policy_chain(*policies: object) -> object:
          """Chain several icon policies: the first non-empty marker wins.
      
          Convenience for layering custom icons on top of the default policy
          without losing the dir3 defaults.  Returns an object with
          ``icon_for(name, index) -> str``; implement the whole trait yourself
          when you need control.
          """
      
          class _Chain:
              def __init__(self, chain):
                  self._chain = chain
      
              def icon_for(self, name: str, index: int) -> str:
                  for policy in self._chain:
                      candidate = getattr(policy, "icon_for", None)
                      if callable(candidate):
                          marker = candidate(name, index)
                          if marker:
                              return marker
                  return ""
      
          return _Chain(list(policies))
      
      
      @dataclass
      class PrayerStatusColorPolicy:
          """Prayers change color with their schedule state.
      
          ``critical`` and ``kerahat`` names are red, names that take time from a
          lecture are orange, exact Adhan-time prayers are green, and ``shifted``
          names are yellow. Everything else falls back to
          :class:`PrayerColorPolicy`.
      
          A planfile opts in with ``color_policy = PrayerStatusColorPolicy()`` and
          names its prayer events accordingly (e.g. ``Asr (verschoben: …)``,
          ``Maghrib (5 min von der Vorlesung)`` or
          ``Isha (kritisch, noch 20 min bis Fajr-Adhan)``).
          """
      
          fallback: ColorPolicy = field(default_factory=PrayerColorPolicy)
      
          def color_for(self, name: str, index: int) -> int | None:
              normalized = normalize_event_name(name)
              head, _, rest = normalized.partition(" ")
              if head in PRAYER_NAMES and (not rest.strip() or rest.lstrip().startswith("(")):
                  if CRITICAL_MARKER in normalized or KERAHAT_MARKER in normalized:
                      return RED_SLOT
                  if ORANGE_MARKER in normalized:
                      return ORANGE_SLOT
                  if SHIFTED_MARKER in normalized:
                      return YELLOW_SLOT
                  return GREEN_SLOT
              return self.fallback.color_for(name, index)
      
      
      class BasilPistazienColorPolicy:
          """Prayer-status colors in the user's chosen palette:
      
          Am Adhan im Moschee → Basilikum
          Verschoben im Moschee → Pistazie
          Am Adhan allein → Avokado
          Verschoben allein → Zitrone
          Im Kerahat → Mandarine
          Kritisch → Tomate
      
          Alles andere fällt auf den Namen-hash zurück.
      
          Das ist dasselbe Logik wie :class:`PrayerStatusColorPolicy`, nur mit
          anderen Slot-Nummern, die auf die gewünschten GCal-Farben abbilden.
          """
      
          # CColor slots remapping to the requested palette
          _basilikum: int = 9   # Basilikum
          _pistazie: int = 10   # Pistazie
          _avokado: int = 3     # Avokado
          _zitrone: int = 1     # Zitrone
          _mandarine: int = 5   # Mandarine
          _tomate: int = 4      # Tomate
      
          fallback: ColorPolicy = field(default_factory=PrayerColorPolicy)
      
          def color_for(self, name: str, index: int) -> int | None:
              normalized = normalize_event_name(name)
              head, sep, rest = normalized.partition(" ")
      
              if head not in PRAYER_NAMES:
                  return self.fallback.color_for(name, index)
      
              # Nur Gebetsnamen mit Klammer-Info analysieren
              if not rest.strip() or not rest.lstrip().startswith("("):
                  # Am Adhan allein (kein Klammern-Inhalt)
                  return self._avokado
      
              # Klammer-Inhalt analysieren
              marker_text = rest.strip().lstrip("(").rstrip(")").lower()
      
              if KERAHAT_MARKER in marker_text:
                  return self._mandarine
      
              if CRITICAL_MARKER in marker_text:
                  return self._tomate
      
              if ORANGE_MARKER in marker_text:
                  return self._avokado  # Am Adhan allein + Vorlesungs-Überlap
      
              if SHIFTED_MARKER in marker_text:
                  # Verschoben - jetzt nach "Moschee" prüfen
                  if "moschee" in marker_text or head == "jumuah":
                      return self._pistazie
                  return self._zitrone
      
              # Am Adhan im Moschee (ohne weitere Markierungen)
              if "moschee" in marker_text:
                  return self._basilikum
      
              # Standard: Am Adhan allein
              return self._avokado
      
      
      @dataclass
      class PlainPolicy:
          """Trait impl: no colors, everything keeps the calendar default."""
      
          def color_for(self, name: str, index: int) -> int | None:
              return None
      
      
      @dataclass
      class DictColorPolicy:
          """Trait impl: explicit ``{event name: colorId}`` mapping + fallback policy.
      
          Mapping values are GCal colorIds (``1``..``11`` as int or str); invalid
          values are ignored and fall through to the fallback.
          """
      
          mapping: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
          fallback: ColorPolicy = field(default_factory=PrayerColorPolicy)
      
          def __post_init__(self) -> None:
              self.slots: dict[str, int] = {}
              for name, value in (self.mapping or {}).items():
                  slot = _slot_from_color_id(value)
                  if slot is not None:
                      self.slots[normalize_event_name(name)] = slot
      
          def color_for(self, name: str, index: int) -> int | None:
              slot = self.slots.get(normalize_event_name(name))
              if slot is not None:
                  return slot
              return self.fallback.color_for(name, index)

  content: |
      """Event colors as a trait-like policy, portable across providers.
      
      Munazzim colors prayers fixed and cycles everything else (TUI-only there).
      dir3 ports the *idea* to real calendar colors: a :class:`ColorPolicy` decides
      *which* color family an event gets (as a neutral slot ``0..10``), each
      provider renders the slot its own way (GCal: ``colorId`` ``"1".."11"``).
      
      Rules (munazzim-inspired): the default policy keeps prayers yellow; the
      optional status policy colors prayers at the Adhan green, shifted prayers
      yellow, prayers that take lecture time orange, and critical prayers red.
      Every other event gets a deterministic color from its name - same name, same
      color.
      
      Implement the trait for custom behavior - any object with
      ``color_for(name, index) -> int | None`` works, no inheritance needed::
      
          class MyColors:
              def color_for(self, name, index):
                  return 10 if "sleep" in name.lower() else None
      """
      from __future__ import annotations
      
      from dataclasses import dataclass, field
      from typing import Protocol, runtime_checkable
      
      
      @runtime_checkable
      class ColorPolicy(Protocol):
          """Trait: maps an event to a color slot ``0..10``, or ``None`` for default."""
      
          def color_for(self, name: str, index: int) -> int | None:
              """Slot for the event with this name at this (per-day) position."""
              ...  # pragma: no cover - trait
      
      
      #: Slot -> GCal ``colorId``. Hand-picked so prayers read naturally
      #: (dawn grape, midday banana, sunset tomato, night blueberry).
      PALETTE = ("3", "6", "5", "7", "11", "9", "1", "2", "4", "8", "10")
      
      #: Normalized prayer names - always rendered yellow (GCal Banana).
      # lange Gebetsnamen -> kurze, informative Varianten für die Anzeige
      SHORT_PRAYER_NAMES: dict[str, str] = {
          "fajr": "Fajr",
          "sunrise": "Sonnenaufgang",
          "dhuhr": "Dhuhr",
          "duhr": "Dhuhr",
          "jumuah": "Jumuah",
          "asr": "Asr",
          "maghrib": "Maghrib",
          "isha": "Isha",
          "sunset": "Sonnenuntergang",
      }
      
      PRAYER_NAMES = frozenset(
          {"fajr", "sunrise", "dhuhr", "duhr", "jumuah", "asr", "maghrib", "isha"}
      )
      
      #: Slot rendering as yellow (GCal Banana ``"5"``) on every provider.
      YELLOW_SLOT = 2
      
      #: Slot rendering as green (GCal Sage ``"2"``) on every provider.
      GREEN_SLOT = 7
      
      #: Slot rendering as red (GCal Tomato ``"11"``) on every provider.
      RED_SLOT = 4
      
      #: Slot rendering as orange (GCal Tangerine ``"6"``) on every provider.
      ORANGE_SLOT = 1
      
      #: Markers a plan can put into a prayer name to describe its schedule state.
      SHIFTED_MARKER = "verschoben"
      CRITICAL_MARKER = "kritisch"
      KERAHAT_MARKER = "kerahat"
      ORANGE_MARKER = "von der vorlesung"
      
      
      def shorten_event_name(name: str | None) -> str:
          """Kürzt lange Event-Namen, ohne Information zu verlieren.
      
          Entfernt:
          - überflüssige Beschreibungen in Klammern, wenn der Kontext klar ist
          - wiederholte Präfixe wie "Weg: " wenn bereits am Anfang
          - redundante Zusätze wie "(Moschee, nur Fardh)" → "(Moschee)"
          - Indexnummern bei Vorlesungen, wenn sie länger als nötig sind
          - verbose Reiseroute-Beschreibungen zu "Weg: A >> B"
      
          Behält aber alle wichtigen Informationen bei: Adhan-Zeiten, Verschiebungen,
          Kerahat-Status, Vorlesungs-Überschneidungen, Fardh/Hadith-Info etc.
          """
          if not name:
              return ""
      
          text = str(name)
          normalized = normalize_event_name(text)
          head, sep, rest = normalized.partition(" ")        # LANGE Vorlesungsnamen kürzen: "EN 732 ROBS (Uebung, Marvin)" → "EN732 ROBS (Ü)"
          # Hinweis: Nur Namen mit Kursnummer-Muster (ABC 123 XYZ) werden gekürzt.
          # Namen wie "HE101 AnalinA (Winkert)" bleiben unverändert.
          if rest.startswith("(") or any(k in rest for k in ("uebung", "übung", "exercise", "exercises", "lab", "labs", "lecture", "lectures", "seminar", "vorlesung")):
              import re
      
              # Kursnummer + Name + Klammerinfo kompaktieren (nur bei Klammer-Inhalten)
              if rest.startswith("("):
                  match = re.match(r"^([a-z]+)\s+(\d+)\s+([a-z0-9]+)\s+\(([^)]+)\)$", text, re.IGNORECASE)
                  if match:
                      prefix, nummer, name_kurz, info = match.groups()
                      info_lower = info.lower()
                      if "uebung" in info_lower or "übung" in info_lower:
                          info = "Ü"
                      elif "exercise" in info_lower or "exercises" in info_lower:
                          info = "Ex"
                      elif "lab" in info_lower or "labs" in info_lower:
                          info = "Lab"
                      elif "lecture" in info_lower or "lectures" in info_lower:
                          info = "V"
                      elif "seminar" in info_lower:
                          info = "S"
                      elif "vorlesung" in info_lower:
                          info = "V"
                      return f"{prefix}{nummer} {name_kurz} ({info})".strip()
              # Fallback: Keine Klammer, also unverändert zurückgeben
              return text    # Weg-Namen kompaktieren: "Weg: Mertensstr. >> Berlin, Galenstr. BUS 136" → "Weg: Mertensstr. >> Berlin"
          if head == "weg" and ">>" in text:
              import re
      
              match = re.match(r"^Weg:\s*(.+?)\s*>>\s*(.+?),?\s*(?:[A-Z]{2,4}\s*\d+)?\s*(?:BUS\s*\d+)?\s*$", text, re.IGNORECASE)
              if match:
                  von = match.group(1).strip()
                  nach = match.group(2).strip()
                  return f"Weg: {von} >> {nach}"
              # Falls das Muster nicht passt (z.B. weil BUS 136 fehlt), gib den Originalnamen zurück
              return text    # Redundante Klammer-Inhalte entfernen
          # Hinweis: "(Moschee)" bleibt als Marker erhalten, da es wichtige Info ist.
          # Nur spezifische redundanten Infos wie "(Moschee, nur Fardh)" werden gekürzt.
          if rest.startswith("("):
              import re
      
              text = re.sub(
                  r"\((\s*)(Moschee|NahMoschee|allein)(,\s*(nur Fardh|nur Hadith|Fardh|Hadith))?(\s*)\)",
                  lambda m: f"({'Moschee' if 'moschee' in m.group(1).lower() or 'nahmoschee' in m.group(1).lower() else 'allein'})",
                  text,
                  flags=re.IGNORECASE,
              )
              # "Fajr (Moschee)" bleibt unverändert, da es kein redundantes Info ist.
      
          return text
      
      
      def event_summary(name: str | None, icon_policy: object | None = None, index: int = 0) -> str:
          """Event-Name mit Icon und gekürztem Text für die Anzeige.
      
          Kombiniert:
          - :func:`shorten_event_name` für die Namensverkürzung
          - :meth:`icon_policy.icon_for` für das Icon (wenn vorhanden)
          
          Rückgabe: ``"🕋 Fajr"`` oder ``"🏫 EN732 ROBS (Ü)"`` etc.
          """
          if not name:
              return ""
      
          short = shorten_event_name(name)
          icon = ""
          if icon_policy is not None:
              icon_fn = getattr(icon_policy, "icon_for", None)
              if callable(icon_fn):
                  icon = icon_fn(name, index) or ""
      
          if icon:
              return f"{icon} {short}"
          return short
      
      
      def normalize_event_name(name: object) -> str:
          return str(name or "").strip().casefold()
      
      
      def name_slot(name: object) -> int:
          """Deterministic color slot from the event name.
      
          The name's bytes are summed as numbers, modulo the palette length -
          so the same name always yields the same slot on every provider::
      
              sum(b"coding") % 11 == 1
          """
          total = sum(normalize_event_name(name).encode("utf-8"))
          return total % len(PALETTE)
      
      
      def to_gcal_color_id(slot: object) -> str | None:
          """Render a policy slot as a GCal ``colorId`` (``None`` = calendar default)."""
          try:
              index = int(slot)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
          except (TypeError, ValueError):
              return None
          if isinstance(slot, bool) or not 0 <= index <= 10:
              return None
          return PALETTE[index]
      
      
      def _slot_from_color_id(value: object) -> int | None:
          """User-facing GCal ``colorId`` (``1``..``11``) -> palette slot (round-trip safe)."""
          if isinstance(value, bool):
              return None
          try:
              text = str(int(str(value).strip()))
          except (TypeError, ValueError):
              return None
          try:
              return PALETTE.index(text)
          except ValueError:
              return None
      
      
      @dataclass
      class PrayerColorPolicy:
          """Default trait impl: prayers yellow, everything else name-hashed."""
      
          def color_for(self, name: str, index: int) -> int | None:
              if normalize_event_name(name) in PRAYER_NAMES:
                  return YELLOW_SLOT
              return name_slot(name)
      
      
      class IconPolicy:
          """Trait: attaches one unicode marker to an event summary.
      
          Markers are orthogonal to colors: :class:`ColorPolicy` picks the
          calendar fill, :class:`IconPolicy` picks the inline glyph that
          readable output and calendar titles carry around.
      
          dir3 bundles a :class:`DefaultIconPolicy` that tags prayers with 🕋,
          lectures/Übungen with 🏫, and travel with 🛣.  Implement the trait
          yourself when you want different icons - any object with
          ``icon_for(name, index) -> str`` works, no inheritance needed::
      
              class MyIcons:
                  def icon_for(self, name, index):
                      return '  📚 ' if 'lecture' in name.lower() else ''
          """
      
          def icon_for(self, name: str, index: int) -> str:
              """Icon marker to prefix an event summary with."""
              ...  # pragma: no cover - trait
      
      
      @dataclass
      class DefaultIconPolicy:
          """Bundled icon policy: 🕋 prayers, 🏫 lectures/Übungen, 🛣 travel.
      
          ``index`` is the per-day position of the event - it lets the policy
          decide differently for the same name in different places if ever
          needed, though the default policy is name-driven.
          """
      
          _icons: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
      
          def __post_init__(self) -> None:
              self._icons.update(
                  **{
                      "": "🕋",  # bare prayer name
                      "fajr": "🕋",
                      "sunrise": "🕋",
                      "dhuhr": "🕋",
                      "duhr": "🕋",
                      "jumuah": "🕋",
                      "asr": "🕋",
                      "maghrib": "🕋",
                      "isha": "🕋",
                  }
              )
      
          def icon_for(self, name: str, index: int) -> str:
              normalized = normalize_event_name(name)
              head, _, rest = normalized.partition(" ")
      
              # bare prayer name (and plain parenthetical variants) → 🕋
              if head in PRAYER_NAMES or (head in PRAYER_NAMES and rest.startswith("(")):
                  return self._icons.get(head, "🕋")
      
              # lectures / Übungen / exercises / labs → 🏫
              if self._looks_like_lecture(rest if head else normalized):
                  return "🏫"
              if self._looks_like_lecture(head):
                  return "🏫"
      
              # travel / journey / way / trip → 🛣
              if self._looks_like_travel(normalized):
                  return "🛣"
      
              return ""
      
          @staticmethod
          def _looks_like_lecture(rest: str) -> bool:
              text = rest.strip().lower()
              if not text:
                  return False
              if text.startswith("("):
                  text = text.strip("() ")
              return any(k in text for k in ("übung", "uebung", "exercise", "exercises", "lab", "labs", "lecture", "lectures", "seminar", "vorlesung"))
      
          @staticmethod
          def _looks_like_travel(name: str) -> bool:
              lowered = name.lower()
              stripped = lowered.strip().strip("() ")
              if any(w in stripped for w in ("weg", "travel", "trip", "journey", "fahrt", "commute", "zurück", "zurueck", "hin", "weg:", "->", ">>")):
                  return True
              return False
      
      
      _CHAIN_ORDER_KEY = "__dir3_icon_chain__"
      
      
      def icon_policy_chain(*policies: object) -> object:
          """Chain several icon policies: the first non-empty marker wins.
      
          Convenience for layering custom icons on top of the default policy
          without losing the dir3 defaults.  Returns an object with
          ``icon_for(name, index) -> str``; implement the whole trait yourself
          when you need control.
          """
      
          class _Chain:
              def __init__(self, chain):
                  self._chain = chain
      
              def icon_for(self, name: str, index: int) -> str:
                  for policy in self._chain:
                      candidate = getattr(policy, "icon_for", None)
                      if callable(candidate):
                          marker = candidate(name, index)
                          if marker:
                              return marker
                  return ""
      
          return _Chain(list(policies))
      
      
      @dataclass
      class PrayerStatusColorPolicy:
          """Prayers change color with their schedule state.
      
          ``critical`` and ``kerahat`` names are red, names that take time from a
          lecture are orange, exact Adhan-time prayers are green, and ``shifted``
          names are yellow. Everything else falls back to
          :class:`PrayerColorPolicy`.
      
          A planfile opts in with ``color_policy = PrayerStatusColorPolicy()`` and
          names its prayer events accordingly (e.g. ``Asr (verschoben: …)``,
          ``Maghrib (5 min von der Vorlesung)`` or
          ``Isha (kritisch, noch 20 min bis Fajr-Adhan)``).
          """
      
          fallback: ColorPolicy = field(default_factory=PrayerColorPolicy)
      
          def color_for(self, name: str, index: int) -> int | None:
              normalized = normalize_event_name(name)
              head, _, rest = normalized.partition(" ")
              if head in PRAYER_NAMES and (not rest.strip() or rest.lstrip().startswith("(")):
                  if CRITICAL_MARKER in normalized or KERAHAT_MARKER in normalized:
                      return RED_SLOT
                  if ORANGE_MARKER in normalized:
                      return ORANGE_SLOT
                  if SHIFTED_MARKER in normalized:
                      return YELLOW_SLOT
                  return GREEN_SLOT
              return self.fallback.color_for(name, index)
      
      
      class BasilPistazienColorPolicy:
          """Prayer-status colors in the user's chosen palette:
      
          Am Adhan im Moschee → Basilikum
          Verschoben im Moschee → Pistazie
          Am Adhan allein → Avokado
          Verschoben allein → Zitrone
          Im Kerahat → Mandarine
          Kritisch → Tomate
      
          Alles andere fällt auf den Namen-hash zurück.
      
          Das ist dasselbe Logik wie :class:`PrayerStatusColorPolicy`, nur mit
          anderen Slot-Nummern, die auf die gewünschten GCal-Farben abbilden.
          """
      
          # Color slots remapping to the requested palette
          _basilikum: int = 9   # Basilikum
          _pistazie: int = 10   # Pistazie
          _avokado: int = 3     # Avokado
          _zitrone: int = 1     # Zitrone
          _mandarine: int = 5   # Mandarine
          _tomate: int = 4      # Tomate
      
          fallback: ColorPolicy | None = field(default=None, init=False, repr=False)
      
          def __post_init__(self) -> None:
              if self.fallback is None:
                  object.__setattr__(self, "fallback", PrayerColorPolicy())
      
          def color_for(self, name: str, index: int) -> int | None:
              normalized = normalize_event_name(name)
              head, sep, rest = normalized.partition(" ")
      
              if head not in PRAYER_NAMES:
                  if self.fallback is not None:
                      return self.fallback.color_for(name, index)
                  return name_slot(name)
      
              # Nur Gebetsnamen mit Klammer-Info analysieren
              if not rest.strip() or not rest.lstrip().startswith("("):
                  # Am Adhan allein (kein Klammern-Inhalt)
                  return self._avokado
      
              # Klammer-Inhalt analysieren
              marker_text = rest.strip().lstrip("(").rstrip(")").lower()
      
              if KERAHAT_MARKER in marker_text:
                  return self._mandarine
      
              if CRITICAL_MARKER in marker_text:
                  return self._tomate
      
              if ORANGE_MARKER in marker_text:
                  return self._avokado  # Am Adhan allein + Vorlesungs-Überlap
      
              if SHIFTED_MARKER in marker_text:
                  # Verschoben - jetzt nach "Moschee" prüfen
                  if "moschee" in marker_text or head == "jumuah":
                      return self._pistazie
                  return self._zitrone
      
              # Am Adhan im Moschee (ohne weitere Markierungen)
              if "moschee" in marker_text:
                  return self._basilikum
      
              # Standard: Am Adhan allein
              return self._avokado
      
      
      @dataclass
      class PlainPolicy:
          """Trait impl: no colors, everything keeps the calendar default."""
      
          def color_for(self, name: str, index: int) -> int | None:
              return None
      
      
      @dataclass
      class DictColorPolicy:
          """Trait impl: explicit ``{event name: colorId}`` mapping + fallback policy.
      
          Mapping values are GCal colorIds (``1``..``11`` as int or str); invalid
          values are ignored and fall through to the fallback.
          """
      
          mapping: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
          fallback: ColorPolicy = field(default_factory=PrayerColorPolicy)
      
          def __post_init__(self) -> None:
              self.slots: dict[str, int] = {}
              for name, value in (self.mapping or {}).items():
                  slot = _slot_from_color_id(value)
                  if slot is not None:
                      self.slots[normalize_event_name(name)] = slot
      
          def color_for(self, name: str, index: int) -> int | None:
              slot = self.slots.get(normalize_event_name(name))
              if slot is not None:
                  return slot
              return self.fallback.color_for(name, index)
      
  referencedBy: {}

- path: src/dir3/color.py
  content: |
      """Event colors as a trait-like policy, portable across providers.
      
      Munazzim colors prayers fixed and cycles everything else (TUI-only there).
      dir3 ports the *idea* to real calendar colors: a :class:`ColorPolicy` decides
      *which* color family an event gets (as a neutral slot ``0..10``), each
      provider renders the slot its own way (GCal: ``colorId`` ``"1".."11"``).
      
      Rules (munazzim-inspired): the default policy keeps prayers yellow; the
      optional status policy colors prayers at the Adhan green, shifted prayers
      yellow, prayers that take lecture time orange, and critical prayers red.
      Every other event gets a deterministic color from its name - same name, same
      color.
      
      Implement the trait for custom behavior - any object with
      ``color_for(name, index) -> int | None`` works, no inheritance needed::
      
          class MyColors:
              def color_for(self, name, index):
                  return 10 if "sleep" in name.lower() else None
      """
      from __future__ import annotations
      
      from dataclasses import dataclass, field
      from typing import Protocol, runtime_checkable
      
      
      @runtime_checkable
      class ColorPolicy(Protocol):
          """Trait: maps an event to a color slot ``0..10``, or ``None`` for default."""
      
          def color_for(self, name: str, index: int) -> int | None:
              """Slot for the event with this name at this (per-day) position."""
              ...  # pragma: no cover - trait
      
      
      #: Slot -> GCal ``colorId``. Hand-picked so prayers read naturally
      #: (dawn grape, midday banana, sunset tomato, night blueberry).
      PALETTE = ("3", "6", "5", "7", "11", "9", "1", "2", "4", "8", "10")
      
      #: Normalized prayer names - always rendered yellow (GCal Banana).
      # lange Gebetsnamen -> kurze, informative Varianten für die Anzeige
      SHORT_PRAYER_NAMES: dict[str, str] = {
          "fajr": "Fajr",
          "sunrise": "Sonnenaufgang",
          "dhuhr": "Dhuhr",
          "duhr": "Dhuhr",
          "jumuah": "Jumuah",
          "asr": "Asr",
          "maghrib": "Maghrib",
          "isha": "Isha",
          "sunset": "Sonnenuntergang",
      }
      
      PRAYER_NAMES = frozenset(
          {"fajr", "sunrise", "dhuhr", "duhr", "jumuah", "asr", "maghrib", "isha"}
      )
      
      #: Slot rendering as yellow (GCal Banana ``"5"``) on every provider.
      YELLOW_SLOT = 2
      
      #: Slot rendering as green (GCal Sage ``"2"``) on every provider.
      GREEN_SLOT = 7
      
      #: Slot rendering as red (GCal Tomato ``"11"``) on every provider.
      RED_SLOT = 4
      
      #: Slot rendering as orange (GCal Tangerine ``"6"``) on every provider.
      ORANGE_SLOT = 1
      
      #: Markers a plan can put into a prayer name to describe its schedule state.
      SHIFTED_MARKER = "verschoben"
      CRITICAL_MARKER = "kritisch"
      KERAHAT_MARKER = "kerahat"
      ORANGE_MARKER = "von der vorlesung"
      
      
      def shorten_event_name(name: str | None) -> str:
          """Kürzt lange Event-Namen, ohne Information zu verlieren.
      
          Entfernt:
          - überflüssige Beschreibungen in Klammern, wenn der Kontext klar ist
          - wiederholte Präfixe wie "Weg: " wenn bereits am Anfang
          - redundante Zusätze wie "(Moschee, nur Fardh)" → "(Moschee)"
          - Indexnummern bei Vorlesungen, wenn sie länger als nötig sind
          - verbose Reiseroute-Beschreibungen zu "Weg: A >> B"
      
          Behält aber alle wichtigen Informationen bei: Adhan-Zeiten, Verschiebungen,
          Kerahat-Status, Vorlesungs-Überschneidungen, Fardh/Hadith-Info etc.
          """
          if not name:
              return ""
      
          text = str(name)
          normalized = normalize_event_name(text)
          head, sep, rest = normalized.partition(" ")        # LANGE Vorlesungsnamen kürzen: "EN 732 ROBS (Uebung, Marvin)" → "EN732 ROBS (Ü)"
          # Hinweis: Nur Namen mit Kursnummer-Muster (ABC 123 XYZ) werden gekürzt.
          # Namen wie "HE101 AnalinA (Winkert)" bleiben unverändert.
              # LANGE Vorlesungsnamen kürzen: "EN 732 ROBS (Uebung, Marvin)" → "EN732 ROBS (Ü)"
          # Hinweis: Nur Namen mit Kursnummer-Muster (ABC 123 XYZ) werden gekürzt.
          # Namen wie "HE101 AnalinA (Winkert)" bleiben unverändert.
              if rest.startswith("(") or any(k in rest for k in ("uebung", "übung", "exercise", "exercises", "lab", "labs", "lecture", "lectures", "seminar", "vorlesung")):
                  import re
      
              # Kursnummer + Name + Klammerinfo kompaktieren (nur bei Klammer-Inhalten)
                  if rest.startswith("("):
                      match = re.match(r"^([a-z]+)\s+(\d+)\s+([a-z0-9]+)\s+\(([^)]+)\)$", text, re.IGNORECASE)
                      if match:
                          prefix, nummer, name_kurz, info = match.groups()
                          info_lower = info.lower()
                          if "uebung" in info_lower or "übung" in info_lower:
                              info = "Ü"
                          elif "exercise" in info_lower or "exercises" in info_lower:
                              info = "Ex"
                          elif "lab" in info_lower or "labs" in info_lower:
                              info = "Lab"
                          elif "lecture" in info_lower or "lectures" in info_lower:
                              info = "V"
                          elif "seminar" in info_lower:
                              info = "S"
                          elif "vorlesung" in info_lower:
                              info = "V"
                          return f"{prefix}{nummer} {name_kurz} ({info})".strip()
                  # Fallback: Keine Klammer, also unverändert zurückgeben
                  return text    # Weg-Namen kompaktieren: "Weg: Mertensstr. >> Berlin, Galenstr. BUS 136" → "Weg: Mertensstr. >> Berlin"
          if head == "weg" and ">>" in text:
              import re
      
              match = re.match(r"^Weg:\s*(.+?)\s*>>\s*(.+?),?\s*(?:[A-Z]{2,4}\s*\d+)?\s*(?:BUS\s*\d+)?\s*$", text, re.IGNORECASE)
              if match:
                  von = match.group(1).strip()
                  nach = match.group(2).strip()
                  return f"Weg: {von} >> {nach}"
              # Falls das Muster nicht passt (z.B. weil BUS 136 fehlt), gib den Originalnamen zurück
              return text    # Redundante Klammer-Inhalte entfernen
          # Hinweis: "(Moschee)" bleibt als Marker erhalten, da es wichtige Info ist.
          # Nur spezifische redundanten Infos wie "(Moschee, nur Fardh)" werden gekürzt.
          if rest.startswith("("):
              import re
      
              text = re.sub(
                  r"\((\s*)(Moschee|NahMoschee|allein)(,\s*(nur Fardh|nur Hadith|Fardh|Hadith))?(\s*)\)",
                  lambda m: f"({'Moschee' if 'moschee' in m.group(1).lower() or 'nahmoschee' in m.group(1).lower() else 'allein'})",
                  text,
                  flags=re.IGNORECASE,
              )
              # "Fajr (Moschee)" bleibt unverändert, da es kein redundantes Info ist.
      
          return text
      
      
      def event_summary(name: str | None, icon_policy: object | None = None, index: int = 0) -> str:
          """Event-Name mit Icon und gekürztem Text für die Anzeige.
      
          Kombiniert:
          - :func:`shorten_event_name` für die Namensverkürzung
          - :meth:`icon_policy.icon_for` für das Icon (wenn vorhanden)
          
          Rückgabe: ``"🕋 Fajr"`` oder ``"🏫 EN732 ROBS (Ü)"`` etc.
          """
          if not name:
              return ""
      
          short = shorten_event_name(name)
          icon = ""
          if icon_policy is not None:
              icon_fn = getattr(icon_policy, "icon_for", None)
              if callable(icon_fn):
                  icon = icon_fn(name, index) or ""
      
          if icon:
              return f"{icon} {short}"
          return short
      
      
      def normalize_event_name(name: object) -> str:
          return str(name or "").strip().casefold()
      
      
      def name_slot(name: object) -> int:
          """Deterministic color slot from the event name.
      
          The name's bytes are summed as numbers, modulo the palette length -
          so the same name always yields the same slot on every provider::
      
              sum(b"coding") % 11 == 1
          """
          total = sum(normalize_event_name(name).encode("utf-8"))
          return total % len(PALETTE)
      
      
      def to_gcal_color_id(slot: object) -> str | None:
          """Render a policy slot as a GCal ``colorId`` (``None`` = calendar default)."""
          try:
              index = int(slot)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
          except (TypeError, ValueError):
              return None
          if isinstance(slot, bool) or not 0 <= index <= 10:
              return None
          return PALETTE[index]
      
      
      def _slot_from_color_id(value: object) -> int | None:
          """User-facing GCal ``colorId`` (``1``..``11``) -> palette slot (round-trip safe)."""
          if isinstance(value, bool):
              return None
          try:
              text = str(int(str(value).strip()))
          except (TypeError, ValueError):
              return None
          try:
              return PALETTE.index(text)
          except ValueError:
              return None
      
      
      @dataclass
      class PrayerColorPolicy:
          """Default trait impl: prayers yellow, everything else name-hashed."""
      
          def color_for(self, name: str, index: int) -> int | None:
              if normalize_event_name(name) in PRAYER_NAMES:
                  return YELLOW_SLOT
              return name_slot(name)
      
      
      class IconPolicy:
          """Trait: attaches one unicode marker to an event summary.
      
          Markers are orthogonal to colors: :class:`ColorPolicy` picks the
          calendar fill, :class:`IconPolicy` picks the inline glyph that
          readable output and calendar titles carry around.
      
          dir3 bundles a :class:`DefaultIconPolicy` that tags prayers with 🕋,
          lectures/Übungen with 🏫, and travel with 🛣.  Implement the trait
          yourself when you want different icons - any object with
          ``icon_for(name, index) -> str`` works, no inheritance needed::
      
              class MyIcons:
                  def icon_for(self, name, index):
                      return '  📚 ' if 'lecture' in name.lower() else ''
          """
      
          def icon_for(self, name: str, index: int) -> str:
              """Icon marker to prefix an event summary with."""
              ...  # pragma: no cover - trait
      
      
      @dataclass
      class DefaultIconPolicy:
          """Bundled icon policy: 🕋 prayers, 🏫 lectures/Übungen, 🛣 travel.
      
          ``index`` is the per-day position of the event - it lets the policy
          decide differently for the same name in different places if ever
          needed, though the default policy is name-driven.
          """
      
          _icons: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
      
          def __post_init__(self) -> None:
              self._icons.update(
                  **{
                      "": "🕋",  # bare prayer name
                      "fajr": "🕋",
                      "sunrise": "🕋",
                      "dhuhr": "🕋",
                      "duhr": "🕋",
                      "jumuah": "🕋",
                      "asr": "🕋",
                      "maghrib": "🕋",
                      "isha": "🕋",
                  }
              )
      
          def icon_for(self, name: str, index: int) -> str:
              normalized = normalize_event_name(name)
              head, _, rest = normalized.partition(" ")
      
              # bare prayer name (and plain parenthetical variants) → 🕋
              if head in PRAYER_NAMES or (head in PRAYER_NAMES and rest.startswith("(")):
                  return self._icons.get(head, "🕋")
      
              # lectures / Übungen / exercises / labs → 🏫
              if self._looks_like_lecture(rest if head else normalized):
                  return "🏫"
              if self._looks_like_lecture(head):
                  return "🏫"
      
              # travel / journey / way / trip → 🛣
              if self._looks_like_travel(normalized):
                  return "🛣"
      
              return ""
      
          @staticmethod
          def _looks_like_lecture(rest: str) -> bool:
              text = rest.strip().lower()
              if not text:
                  return False
              if text.startswith("("):
                  text = text.strip("() ")
              return any(k in text for k in ("übung", "uebung", "exercise", "exercises", "lab", "labs", "lecture", "lectures", "seminar", "vorlesung"))
      
          @staticmethod
          def _looks_like_travel(name: str) -> bool:
              lowered = name.lower()
              stripped = lowered.strip().strip("() ")
              if any(w in stripped for w in ("weg", "travel", "trip", "journey", "fahrt", "commute", "zurück", "zurueck", "hin", "weg:", "->", ">>")):
                  return True
              return False
      
      
      _CHAIN_ORDER_KEY = "__dir3_icon_chain__"
      
      
      def icon_policy_chain(*policies: object) -> object:
          """Chain several icon policies: the first non-empty marker wins.
      
          Convenience for layering custom icons on top of the default policy
          without losing the dir3 defaults.  Returns an object with
          ``icon_for(name, index) -> str``; implement the whole trait yourself
          when you need control.
          """
      
          class _Chain:
              def __init__(self, chain):
                  self._chain = chain
      
              def icon_for(self, name: str, index: int) -> str:
                  for policy in self._chain:
                      candidate = getattr(policy, "icon_for", None)
                      if callable(candidate):
                          marker = candidate(name, index)
                          if marker:
                              return marker
                  return ""
      
          return _Chain(list(policies))
      
      
      @dataclass
      class PrayerStatusColorPolicy:
          """Prayers change color with their schedule state.
      
          ``critical`` and ``kerahat`` names are red, names that take time from a
          lecture are orange, exact Adhan-time prayers are green, and ``shifted``
          names are yellow. Everything else falls back to
          :class:`PrayerColorPolicy`.
      
          A planfile opts in with ``color_policy = PrayerStatusColorPolicy()`` and
          names its prayer events accordingly (e.g. ``Asr (verschoben: …)``,
          ``Maghrib (5 min von der Vorlesung)`` or
          ``Isha (kritisch, noch 20 min bis Fajr-Adhan)``).
          """
      
          fallback: ColorPolicy = field(default_factory=PrayerColorPolicy)
      
          def color_for(self, name: str, index: int) -> int | None:
              normalized = normalize_event_name(name)
              head, _, rest = normalized.partition(" ")
              if head in PRAYER_NAMES and (not rest.strip() or rest.lstrip().startswith("(")):
                  if CRITICAL_MARKER in normalized or KERAHAT_MARKER in normalized:
                      return RED_SLOT
                  if ORANGE_MARKER in normalized:
                      return ORANGE_SLOT
                  if SHIFTED_MARKER in normalized:
                      return YELLOW_SLOT
                  return GREEN_SLOT
              return self.fallback.color_for(name, index)
      
      
      class BasilPistazienColorPolicy:
          """Prayer-status colors in the user's chosen palette:
      
          Am Adhan im Moschee → Basilikum
          Verschoben im Moschee → Pistazie
          Am Adhan allein → Avokado
          Verschoben allein → Zitrone
          Im Kerahat → Mandarine
          Kritisch → Tomate
      
          Alles andere fällt auf den Namen-hash zurück.
      
          Das ist dasselbe Logik wie :class:`PrayerStatusColorPolicy`, nur mit
          anderen Slot-Nummern, die auf die gewünschten GCal-Farben abbilden.
          """
      
          # Color slots remapping to the requested palette
          _basilikum: int = 9   # Basilikum
          _pistazie: int = 10   # Pistazie
          _avokado: int = 3     # Avokado
          _zitrone: int = 1     # Zitrone
          _mandarine: int = 5   # Mandarine
          _tomate: int = 4      # Tomate
      
          fallback: ColorPolicy | None = field(default=None, init=False, repr=False)
      
          def __post_init__(self) -> None:
              if self.fallback is None:
                  object.__setattr__(self, "fallback", PrayerColorPolicy())
      
          def color_for(self, name: str, index: int) -> int | None:
              normalized = normalize_event_name(name)
              head, sep, rest = normalized.partition(" ")
      
              if head not in PRAYER_NAMES:
                  if self.fallback is not None:
                      return self.fallback.color_for(name, index)
                  return name_slot(name)
      
              # Nur Gebetsnamen mit Klammer-Info analysieren
              if not rest.strip() or not rest.lstrip().startswith("("):
                  # Am Adhan allein (kein Klammern-Inhalt)
                  return self._avokado
      
              # Klammer-Inhalt analysieren
              marker_text = rest.strip().lstrip("(").rstrip(")").lower()
      
              if KERAHAT_MARKER in marker_text:
                  return self._mandarine
      
              if CRITICAL_MARKER in marker_text:
                  return self._tomate
      
              if ORANGE_MARKER in marker_text:
                  return self._avokado  # Am Adhan allein + Vorlesungs-Überlap
      
              if SHIFTED_MARKER in marker_text:
                  # Verschoben - jetzt nach "Moschee" prüfen
                  if "moschee" in marker_text or head == "jumuah":
                      return self._pistazie
                  return self._zitrone
      
              # Am Adhan im Moschee (ohne weitere Markierungen)
              if "moschee" in marker_text:
                  return self._basilikum
      
              # Standard: Am Adhan allein
              return self._avokado
      
      
      @dataclass
      class PlainPolicy:
          """Trait impl: no colors, everything keeps the calendar default."""
      
          def color_for(self, name: str, index: int) -> int | None:
              return None
      
      
      @dataclass
      class DictColorPolicy:
          """Trait impl: explicit ``{event name: colorId}`` mapping + fallback policy.
      
          Mapping values are GCal colorIds (``1``..``11`` as int or str); invalid
          values are ignored and fall through to the fallback.
          """
      
          mapping: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
          fallback: ColorPolicy = field(default_factory=PrayerColorPolicy)
      
          def __post_init__(self) -> None:
              self.slots: dict[str, int] = {}
              for name, value in (self.mapping or {}).items():
                  slot = _slot_from_color_id(value)
                  if slot is not None:
                      self.slots[normalize_event_name(name)] = slot
      
          def color_for(self, name: str, index: int) -> int | None:
              slot = self.slots.get(normalize_event_name(name))
              if slot is not None:
                  return slot
              return self.fallback.color_for(name, index)

  content: |
      """Google Calendar sync via aiogoogle (async).
      
      Der Sync schiebt einen kompilierten :class:`Plan` als Events in Google
      Calendar.  Credentials liegen im Python-Planfile (``gcal = GoogleCalendar(...)``)
      - gleiche Philosophie wie der Rest von dir3.
      
      Idempotenz: jedes Event bekommt eine deterministische Custom-ID (plain
      SHA1-Hex über Titel/Tag/Name/Zeiten).  Die ID steht im Insert-Body
      (base32hex-konform), also meldet ein erneuter Lauf desselben Plans ``409``
      und aktualisiert (PUT) statt zu duplizieren.
      
      Parallelitaet: Jeder Tag bekommt seine eigene Upload-Task - alle Tage laufen
      gleichzeitig (``asyncio.gather``), begrenzt durch ``max_parallel_days``.
      Innerhalb eines Tages fliegen Inserts/Updates als aiogoogle-Batches
      (``as_user(*requests)``, max. ``BATCH_SIZE`` pro Batch) gleichzeitig raus.
      
      Auth (OAuth2, via aiogoogle):
        * ``refresh_token`` + ``client_id``/``client_secret`` -> automatischer
          Refresh beim ersten Request des Laufs;
        * oder ein bereits ausgestelltes ``access_token`` wird direkt benutzt.
      """
      from __future__ import annotations
      
      import asyncio
      import hashlib
      from collections.abc import AsyncIterator, Callable
      from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
      from dataclasses import dataclass
      from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
      
      from aiogoogle import Aiogoogle
      from aiogoogle.auth.creds import ClientCreds, UserCreds
      
      from ..color import ColorPolicy, DefaultIconPolicy, PrayerColorPolicy, to_gcal_color_id
      from ..config import GoogleCalendar
      from .geo import _resolve_tz
      
      #: Minimaler Umfang - dir3 legt nur Events an/aktualisiert sie, liest nie.
      SCOPES = ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.events"]
      
      #: Direkt gegebenes Access-Token gilt für den (kurzen) Sync-Lauf als frisch,
      #: damit aiogoogle keinen Refresh ohne Refresh-Token versucht.
      _ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL = timedelta(hours=1)
      
      
      @dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
      class StagedEvent:
          event_id: str
          summary: str
          body: dict[str, object]
          when: str
          day: str = ""
      
      
      @dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
      class GCalSyncReport:
          total: int
          created: int
          updated: int
          dry_run: bool
      
          def __str__(self) -> str:
              verb = "geplant" if self.dry_run else "synchronisiert"
              noun = "Event" if self.total == 1 else "Events"
              parts = [f"GCal: {self.total} {noun} {verb}"]
              if not self.dry_run:
                  parts.append(f"{self.created} neu, {self.updated} aktualisiert")
              return " · ".join(parts)
      
      
      @dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
      class GCalClearReport:
          deleted: int
          dry_run: bool
      
          def __str__(self) -> str:
              noun = "Event" if self.deleted == 1 else "Events"
              if self.dry_run:
                  return f"GCal: wuerde {self.deleted} {noun} loeschen"
              return f"GCal: {self.deleted} {noun} geloescht"
      
      
      def _creds_for(settings: GoogleCalendar) -> tuple[UserCreds, ClientCreds | None]:
          """aiogoogle-Credentials aus den Planfile-Einstellungen bauen."""
          if settings.access_token:
              user_creds = UserCreds(
                  access_token=settings.access_token,
                  expires_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc) + _ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL,
              )
              return user_creds, None
          user_creds = UserCreds(refresh_token=settings.refresh_token)
          client_creds = ClientCreds(
              client_id=settings.client_id,
              client_secret=settings.client_secret,
              scopes=list(SCOPES),
          )
          return user_creds, client_creds
      
      
      @asynccontextmanager
      async def _open_client(
          settings: GoogleCalendar, timeout: float
      ) -> AsyncIterator[tuple[Aiogoogle, object]]:
          """Echte aiogoogle-Verbindung: Session + entdeckte Calendar-API liefern."""
          user_creds, client_creds = _creds_for(settings)
          async with Aiogoogle(user_creds=user_creds, client_creds=client_creds) as google:
              yield google, await google.discover("calendar", "v3")
      
      
      #: Öffnet ``(aiogoogle, calendar_api)`` - in Tests durch einen Fake ersetzbar.
      ClientFactory = Callable[[GoogleCalendar, float], object]
      
      #: Max. Events pro aiogoogle-Batch - ein Batch fliegt parallel raus
      #: (``as_user(*requests)``), Batches laufen nacheinander (API-Hoeflichkeit).
      BATCH_SIZE = 11
      
      #: Status, die einen Retry mit Backoff verdienen (Rate-Limits / flaky Server).
      _RETRYABLE_STATUS = {429, 500, 502, 503, 504}
      
      #: Retry-Versuche pro Batch + Start-Delay (verdoppelt sich pro Versuch).
      _MAX_TRIES = 4
      _RETRY_BASE_DELAY = 2.0
      
      
      def _is_rate_limited(res) -> bool:
          """True bei 403ern mit Rate-Limit-Grund (kein Auth-Problem)."""
          payload = getattr(res, "json", None) or {}
          if isinstance(payload, dict):
              error = payload.get("error") or {}
              details = error.get("errors") or []
              for detail in details:
                  if not isinstance(detail, dict):
                      continue
                  if "ratelimit" in str(detail.get("reason", "")).lower():
                      return True
              message = str(error.get("message", "")).lower()
              if "rate limit" in message or "ratelimit" in message:
                  return True
          text = str(getattr(res, "data", "") or "").lower()
          return "rate limit" in text or "ratelimit" in text
      
      
      def _response_kind(res) -> str:
          """``ok`` | ``conflict`` (409) | ``gone`` (404/410) | ``retry`` | ``fatal``."""
          code = res.status_code
          if 200 <= code < 300:
              return "ok"
          if code == 409:
              return "conflict"
          if code in (404, 410):
              return "gone"
          if code in _RETRYABLE_STATUS or (code == 403 and _is_rate_limited(res)):
              return "retry"
          return "fatal"
      
      
      async def _send_requests(google, pairs, *, timeout) -> list:
          """``(item, request)``-Batch senden, mit Retry bei Rate-Limits.
      
          Gibt fertige ``(item, response)``-Paare zurück (409/404/410 sind normale
          Outcomes, kein Retry); fatale Fehler raisen via ``res.raise_for_status()``.
          """
          pending = list(pairs)
          if not pending:
              return []
          finished = []
          delay = _RETRY_BASE_DELAY
          for attempt in range(_MAX_TRIES):
              last = attempt == _MAX_TRIES - 1
              responses = await google.as_user(
                  *(req for _, req in pending),
                  timeout=timeout,
                  full_res=True,
                  raise_for_status=False,
              )
              if not isinstance(responses, list):
                  responses = [responses]
              still = []
              for (item, _req), res in zip(pending, responses):
                  kind = _response_kind(res)
                  if kind == "retry" and not last:
                      still.append((item, _req))
                  elif kind == "fatal" or kind == "retry":
                      res.raise_for_status()
                  else:
                      finished.append((item, res))
              pending = still
              if not pending:
                  return finished
              await asyncio.sleep(delay)
              delay *= 2
          raise AssertionError("unerreichbar - letzter Versuch raist oder beendet immer")
      
      
      def _chunks(items: list, size: int):
          for index in range(0, len(items), size):
              yield items[index : index + size]
      
      
      class GoogleCalendarSyncer:
          def __init__(
              self,
              settings: GoogleCalendar,
              *,
              client_factory: ClientFactory | None = None,
              timeout: float = 10.0,
              max_parallel_days: int = 8,
              color_policy: ColorPolicy | None = None,
              icon_policy: object | None = None,
          ) -> None:
              self.settings = settings
              self._client_factory = client_factory or _open_client
              self.timeout = timeout
              self.max_parallel_days = max_parallel_days
              self._color_policy = color_policy or PrayerColorPolicy()
              self._icon_policy = icon_policy or DefaultIconPolicy()
              self._position = 0  # Für die Position im Event-Stack
      
          def stage(self, plan, *, timezone_name: str) -> list[StagedEvent]:
              """Alle aktiven Events als GCal-Payloads aufbauen (rein, kein Netzwerk).
      
              Der Engine arbeitet in Plan-Wanduhrzeit (naive datetimes); hier wird die
              Plan-Zeitzone attachiert, damit GCal absolute Zeitpunkte bekommt.
              """
              tz = _resolve_tz(timezone_name or "UTC")
              tz_label = getattr(tz, "key", None) or "UTC"
              staged: list[StagedEvent] = []
              for day_ in plan.days:
                  if not day_.active:
                      continue
                  position = 0
                  for ev in day_.events:
                      if not ev.active:
                          continue
                      start = _aware(ev.start, tz)
                      end = _aware(ev.end, tz)
                      fingerprint = "|".join(
                          (plan.title, day_.date.isoformat(), ev.name, start.isoformat(), end.isoformat())
                      )
                      event_id = hashlib.sha1(fingerprint.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
                      # Event-Zusammenfassung: gekürzter Name + Icon aus der IconPolicy
                      body_summary = event_summary(ev.name, self._icon_policy, self._position)
                      self._position += 1
                      body = {
                          "id": event_id,
                          "summary": body_summary,
                          "start": {"dateTime": start.isoformat(), "timeZone": tz_label},
                          "end": {"dateTime": end.isoformat(), "timeZone": tz_label},
                          "description": f"dir3 · {plan.title}",
                          "extendedProperties": {"private": {"dir3": "1"}},
                      }
                      color_id = to_gcal_color_id(self._color_policy.color_for(ev.name, position))
                      if color_id is not None:
                          body["colorId"] = color_id
                      position += 1
      
                      staged.append(
                          StagedEvent(
                              event_id=event_id,
                              summary=body_summary,
                              body=body,
                              when=start.isoformat(),
                              day=day_.date.isoformat(),
                          )
                      )
              staged.sort(key=lambda event: event.when)
              return staged
      
          async def sync(
              self,
              plan,
              *,
              timezone_name: str,
              dry_run: bool = False,
          ) -> GCalSyncReport:
              staged = self.stage(plan, timezone_name=timezone_name)
              if dry_run or not staged:
                  return GCalSyncReport(total=len(staged), created=0, updated=0, dry_run=dry_run)
      
              calendar_id = self.settings.calendar_id
              by_day: dict[str, list[StagedEvent]] = {}
              for event in staged:
                  by_day.setdefault(event.day, []).append(event)
      
              semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(max(1, self.max_parallel_days))
              results: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
              async with self._client_factory(self.settings, self.timeout) as (google, calendar):
      
                  async def run_day(day_events: list[StagedEvent]) -> tuple[int, int]:
                      async with semaphore:
                          made, changed = 0, 0
                          for chunk in _chunks(day_events, BATCH_SIZE):
                              pairs = [
                                  (
                                      event,
                                      calendar.events.insert(
                                          calendarId=calendar_id, json=dict(event.body)
                                      ),
                                  )
                                  for event in chunk
                              ]
                              pending = []
                              for event, res in await _send_requests(
                                  google, pairs, timeout=self.timeout
                              ):
                                  if _response_kind(res) == "conflict":
                                      pending.append(event)
                                  else:
                                      made += 1
                              if pending:
                                  updates = [
                                      (
                                          event,
                                          calendar.events.update(
                                              calendarId=calendar_id,
                                              eventId=event.event_id,
                                              json=dict(event.body),
                                          ),
                                      )
                                      for event in pending
                                  ]
                                  changed += len(
                                      await _send_requests(google, updates, timeout=self.timeout)
                                  )
                          return made, changed
      
                  results = list(
                      await asyncio.gather(*(run_day(events) for events in by_day.values()))
                  )
              created = sum(made for made, _ in results)
              updated = sum(changed for _, changed in results)
              return GCalSyncReport(total=len(staged), created=created, updated=updated, dry_run=False)
      
          async def _list_ids(self, extra_params: dict) -> list[str]:
              """Event-IDs seitenweise einsammeln (Masters - direkt loeschbar)."""
              calendar_id = self.settings.calendar_id
              ids: list[str] = []
              page_token = None
              async with self._client_factory(self.settings, self.timeout) as (google, calendar):
                  while True:
                      params = {
                          "calendarId": calendar_id,
                          "maxResults": 2500,
                          "fields": "nextPageToken,items(id)",
                      }
                      params.update(extra_params)
                      if page_token:
                          params["pageToken"] = page_token
                      data = await google.as_user(
                          calendar.events.list(**params), timeout=self.timeout
                      )
                      ids.extend(item["id"] for item in data.get("items", []) if item.get("id"))
                      page_token = data.get("nextPageToken")
                      if not page_token:
                          return ids
      
          async def list_dir3_event_ids(self) -> list[str]:
              """Alle Events, die dir3 angelegt hat (Marker ``private.dir3=1``)."""
              return await self._list_ids(
                  {"singleEvents": True, "privateExtendedProperty": "dir3=1"}
              )
      
          async def list_all_event_ids(self) -> list[str]:
              """Alle Event-IDs im Kalender (fremde inklusive) - für ``--nuke``."""
              return await self._list_ids({})
      
          async def clear(self, *, dry_run: bool = False, nuke: bool = False) -> GCalClearReport:
              if nuke:
                  ids = await self.list_all_event_ids()
              else:
                  ids = await self.list_dir3_event_ids()
              if dry_run or not ids:
                  return GCalClearReport(deleted=len(ids), dry_run=dry_run)
              calendar_id = self.settings.calendar_id
              deleted = 0
              async with self._client_factory(self.settings, self.timeout) as (google, calendar):
                  for chunk in _chunks(ids, BATCH_SIZE):
                      pairs = [
                          (
                              event_id,
                              calendar.events.delete(calendarId=calendar_id, eventId=event_id),
                          )
                          for event_id in chunk
                      ]
                      # ok + gone (404/410, schon weg) zählen als erledigt
                      deleted += len(await _send_requests(google, pairs, timeout=self.timeout))
              return GCalClearReport(deleted=deleted, dry_run=False)
      
      
      def run_sync(syncer: GoogleCalendarSyncer, plan, *, timezone_name: str, dry_run: bool = False):
          """Sync-Wrapper für den synchronen CLI-Pfad."""
          return asyncio.run(syncer.sync(plan, timezone_name=timezone_name, dry_run=dry_run))
      
      
      def run_clear(syncer: GoogleCalendarSyncer, *, dry_run: bool = False, nuke: bool = False):
          """Clear-Wrapper für den synchronen CLI-Pfad."""
          return asyncio.run(syncer.clear(dry_run=dry_run, nuke=nuke))
      
      
      def _aware(dt, tz):
          return dt.astimezone(tz) if dt.tzinfo is not None else dt.replace(tzinfo=tz)
