```
  content: |
      """Google Calendar sync via aiogoogle (async).
      
      Der Sync schiebt einen kompilierten :class:`Plan` als Events in Google
      Calendar.  Credentials liegen im Python-Planfile (``gcal = GoogleCalendar(...)``)
      - gleiche Philosophie wie der Rest von dir3.
      
      Idempotenz: jedes Event bekommt eine deterministische Custom-ID (plain
      SHA1-Hex über Titel/Tag/Name/Zeiten).  Die ID steht im Insert-Body
      (base32hex-konform), also meldet ein erneuter Lauf desselben Plans ``409``
      und aktualisiert (PUT) statt zu duplizieren.
      
      Parallelitaet: Jeder Tag bekommt seine eigene Upload-Task - alle Tage laufen
      gleichzeitig (``asyncio.gather``), begrenzt durch ``max_parallel_days``.
      Innerhalb eines Tages fliegen Inserts/Updates als aiogoogle-Batches
      (``as_user(*requests)``, max. ``BATCH_SIZE`` pro Batch) gleichzeitig raus.
      
      Auth (OAuth2, via aiogoogle):
        * ``refresh_token`` + ``client_id``/``client_secret`` -> automatischer
          Refresh beim ersten Request des Laufs;
        * oder ein bereits ausgestelltes ``access_token`` wird direkt benutzt.
      """
      from __future__ import annotations
      
      import asyncio
      import hashlib
      from collections.abc import AsyncIterator, Callable
      from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
      from dataclasses import dataclass
      from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
      
      from aiogoogle import Aiogoogle
      from aiogoogle.auth.creds import ClientCreds, UserCreds
      
      from ..color import ColorPolicy, DefaultIconPolicy, PrayerColorPolicy, to_gcal_color_id
      from ..config import GoogleCalendar
      from .geo import _resolve_tz
      
      #: Minimaler Umfang - dir3 legt nur Events an/aktualisiert sie, liest nie.
      SCOPES = ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.events"]
      
      #: Direkt gegebenes Access-Token gilt für den (kurzen) Sync-Lauf als frisch,
      #: damit aiogoogle keinen Refresh ohne Refresh-Token versucht.
      _ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL = timedelta(hours=1)
      
      
      @dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
      class StagedEvent:
          event_id: str
          summary: str
          body: dict[str, object]
          when: str
          day: str = ""
      
      
      @dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
      class GCalSyncReport:
          total: int
          created: int
          updated: int
          dry_run: bool
      
          def __str__(self) -> str:
              verb = "geplant" if self.dry_run else "synchronisiert"
              noun = "Event" if self.total == 1 else "Events"
              parts = [f"GCal: {self.total} {noun} {verb}"]
              if not self.dry_run:
                  parts.append(f"{self.created} neu, {self.updated} aktualisiert")
              return " · ".join(parts)
      
      
      @dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
      class GCalClearReport:
          deleted: int
          dry_run: bool
      
          def __str__(self) -> str:
              noun = "Event" if self.deleted == 1 else "Events"
              if self.dry_run:
                  return f"GCal: wuerde {self.deleted} {noun} loeschen"
              return f"GCal: {self.deleted} {noun} geloescht"
      
      
      def _creds_for(settings: GoogleCalendar) -> tuple[UserCreds, ClientCreds | None]:
          """aiogoogle-Credentials aus den Planfile-Einstellungen bauen."""
          if settings.access_token:
              user_creds = UserCreds(
                  access_token=settings.access_token,
                  expires_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc) + _ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL,
              )
              return user_creds, None
          user_creds = UserCreds(refresh_token=settings.refresh_token)
          client_creds = ClientCreds(
              client_id=settings.client_id,
              client_secret=settings.client_secret,
              scopes=list(SCOPES),
          )
          return user_creds, client_creds
      
      
      @asynccontextmanager
      async def _open_client(
          settings: GoogleCalendar, timeout: float
      ) -> AsyncIterator[tuple[Aiogoogle, object]]:
          """Echte aiogoogle-Verbindung: Session + entdeckte Calendar-API liefern."""
          user_creds, client_creds = _creds_for(settings)
          async with Aiogoogle(user_creds=user_creds, client_creds=client_creds) as google:
              yield google, await google.discover("calendar", "v3")
      
      
      #: Öffnet ``(aiogoogle, calendar_api)`` - in Tests durch einen Fake ersetzbar.
      ClientFactory = Callable[[GoogleCalendar, float], object]
      
      #: Max. Events pro aiogoogle-Batch - ein Batch fliegt parallel raus
      #: (``as_user(*requests)``), Batches laufen nacheinander (API-Hoeflichkeit).
      BATCH_SIZE = 11
      
      #: Status, die einen Retry mit Backoff verdienen (Rate-Limits / flaky Server).
      _RETRYABLE_STATUS = {429, 500, 502, 503, 504}
      
      #: Retry-Versuche pro Batch + Start-Delay (verdoppelt sich pro Versuch).
      _MAX_TRIES = 4
      _RETRY_BASE_DELAY = 2.0
      
      
      def _is_rate_limited(res) -> bool:
          """True bei 403ern mit Rate-Limit-Grund (kein Auth-Problem)."""
          payload = getattr(res, "json", None) or {}
          if isinstance(payload, dict):
              error = payload.get("error") or {}
              details = error.get("errors") or []
              for detail in details:
                  if not isinstance(detail, dict):
                      continue
                  if "ratelimit" in str(detail.get("reason", "")).lower():
                      return True
              message = str(error.get("message", "")).lower()
              if "rate limit" in message or "ratelimit" in message:
                  return True
          text = str(getattr(res, "data", "") or "").lower()
          return "rate limit" in text or "ratelimit" in text
      
      
      def _response_kind(res) -> str:
          """``ok`` | ``conflict`` (409) | ``gone`` (404/410) | ``retry`` | ``fatal``."""
          code = res.status_code
          if 200 <= code < 300:
              return "ok"
          if code == 409:
              return "conflict"
          if code in (404, 410):
              return "gone"
          if code in _RETRYABLE_STATUS or (code == 403 and _is_rate_limited(res)):
              return "retry"
          return "fatal"
      
      
      async def _send_requests(google, pairs, *, timeout) -> list:
          """``(item, request)``-Batch senden, mit Retry bei Rate-Limits.
      
          Gibt fertige ``(item, response)``-Paare zurück (409/404/410 sind normale
          Outcomes, kein Retry); fatale Fehler raisen via ``res.raise_for_status()``.
          """
          pending = list(pairs)
          if not pending:
              return []
          finished = []
          delay = _RETRY_BASE_DELAY
          for attempt in range(_MAX_TRIES):
              last = attempt == _MAX_TRIES - 1
              responses = await google.as_user(
                  *(req for _, req in pending),
                  timeout=timeout,
                  full_res=True,
                  raise_for_status=False,
              )
              if not isinstance(responses, list):
                  responses = [responses]
              still = []
              for (item, _req), res in zip(pending, responses):
                  kind = _response_kind(res)
                  if kind == "retry" and not last:
                      still.append((item, _req))
                  elif kind == "fatal" or kind == "retry":
                      res.raise_for_status()
                  else:
                      finished.append((item, res))
              pending = still
              if not pending:
                  return finished
              await asyncio.sleep(delay)
              delay *= 2
          raise AssertionError("unerreichbar - letzter Versuch raist oder beendet immer")
      
      
      def _chunks(items: list, size: int):
          for index in range(0, len(items), size):
              yield items[index : index + size]
      
      
      class GoogleCalendarSyncer:
          def __init__(
              self,
              settings: GoogleCalendar,
              *,
              client_factory: ClientFactory | None = None,
              timeout: float = 10.0,
              max_parallel_days: int = 8,
              color_policy: ColorPolicy | None = None,
              icon_policy: object | None = None,
          ) -> None:
              self.settings = settings
              self._client_factory = client_factory or _open_client
              self.timeout = timeout
              self.max_parallel_days = max_parallel_days
              self._color_policy = color_policy or PrayerColorPolicy()
              self._icon_policy = icon_policy or DefaultIconPolicy()
              self._position = 0  # Für die Position im Event-Stack
      
          def stage(self, plan, *, timezone_name: str) -> list[StagedEvent]:
              """Alle aktiven Events als GCal-Payloads aufbauen (rein, kein Netzwerk).
      
              Der Engine arbeitet in Plan-Wanduhrzeit (naive datetimes); hier wird die
              Plan-Zeitzone attachiert, damit GCal absolute Zeitpunkte bekommt.
              """
              tz = _resolve_tz(timezone_name or "UTC")
              tz_label = getattr(tz, "key", None) or "UTC"
              staged: list[StagedEvent] = []
              for day_ in plan.days:
                  if not day_.active:
                      continue
                  position = 0
                  for ev in day_.events:
                      if not ev.active:
                          continue
                      start = _aware(ev.start, tz)
                      end = _aware(ev.end, tz)
                      fingerprint = "|".join(
                          (plan.title, day_.date.isoformat(), ev.name, start.isoformat(), end.isoformat())
                      )
                      event_id = hashlib.sha1(fingerprint.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
                      # Event-Zusammenfassung: gekürzter Name + Icon aus der IconPolicy
                      # Event-Zusammenfassung: gekürzter Name + Icon aus der IconPolicy
                      body_summary = event_summary(ev.name, self._icon_policy, position)
                      self._position += 1
                      body = {
                          "id": event_id,
                          "summary": body_summary,
                          "start": {"dateTime": start.isoformat(), "timeZone": tz_label},
                          "end": {"dateTime": end.isoformat(), "timeZone": tz_label},
                          "description": f"dir3 · {plan.title}",
                          "extendedProperties": {"private": {"dir3": "1"}},
                      }
                      color_id = to_gcal_color_id(self._color_policy.color_for(ev.name, position))
                      if color_id is not None:
                          body["colorId"] = color_id
                      position += 1
      
                      staged.append(
                          StagedEvent(
                              event_id=event_id,
                              summary=body_summary,
                              body=body,
                              when=start.isoformat(),
                              day=day_.date.isoformat(),
                          )
                      )
              staged.sort(key=lambda event: event.when)
              return staged
      
          async def sync(
              self,
              plan,
              *,
              timezone_name: str,
              dry_run: bool = False,
          ) -> GCalSyncReport:
              staged = self.stage(plan, timezone_name=timezone_name)
              if dry_run or not staged:
                  return GCalSyncReport(total=len(staged), created=0, updated=0, dry_run=dry_run)
      
              calendar_id = self.settings.calendar_id
              by_day: dict[str, list[StagedEvent]] = {}
              for event in staged:
                  by_day.setdefault(event.day, []).append(event)
      
              semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(max(1, self.max_parallel_days))
              results: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
              async with self._client_factory(self.settings, self.timeout) as (google, calendar):
      
                  async def run_day(day_events: list[StagedEvent]) -> tuple[int, int]:
                      async with semaphore:
                          made, changed = 0, 0
                          for chunk in _chunks(day_events, BATCH_SIZE):
                              pairs = [
                                  (
                                      event,
                                      calendar.events.insert(
                                          calendarId=calendar_id, json=dict(event.body)
                                      ),
                                  )
                                  for event in chunk
                              ]
                              pending = []
                              for event, res in await _send_requests(
                                  google, pairs, timeout=self.timeout
                              ):
                                  if _response_kind(res) == "conflict":
                                      pending.append(event)
                                  else:
                                      made += 1
                              if pending:
                                  updates = [
                                      (
                                          event,
                                          calendar.events.update(
                                              calendarId=calendar_id,
                                              eventId=event.event_id,
                                              json=dict(event.body),
                                          ),
                                      )
                                      for event in pending
                                  ]
                                  changed += len(
                                      await _send_requests(google, updates, timeout=self.timeout)
                                  )
                          return made, changed
      
                  results = list(
                      await asyncio.gather(*(run_day(events) for events in by_day.values()))
                  )
              created = sum(made for made, _ in results)
              updated = sum(changed for _, changed in results)
              return GCalSyncReport(total=len(staged), created=created, updated=updated, dry_run=False)
      
          async def _list_ids(self, extra_params: dict) -> list[str]:
              """Event-IDs seitenweise einsammeln (Masters - direkt loeschbar)."""
              calendar_id = self.settings.calendar_id
              ids: list[str] = []
              page_token = None
              async with self._client_factory(self.settings, self.timeout) as (google, calendar):
                  while True:
                      params = {
                          "calendarId": calendar_id,
                          "maxResults": 2500,
                          "fields": "nextPageToken,items(id)",
                      }
                      params.update(extra_params)
                      if page_token:
                          params["pageToken"] = page_token
                      data = await google.as_user(
                          calendar.events.list(**params), timeout=self.timeout
                      )
                      ids.extend(item["id"] for item in data.get("items", []) if item.get("id"))
                      page_token = data.get("nextPageToken")
                      if not page_token:
                          return ids
      
          async def list_dir3_event_ids(self) -> list[str]:
              """Alle Events, die dir3 angelegt hat (Marker ``private.dir3=1``)."""
              return await self._list_ids(
                  {"singleEvents": True, "privateExtendedProperty": "dir3=1"}
              )
      
          async def list_all_event_ids(self) -> list[str]:
              """Alle Event-IDs im Kalender (fremde inklusive) - für ``--nuke``."""
              return await self._list_ids({})
      
          async def clear(self, *, dry_run: bool = False, nuke: bool = False) -> GCalClearReport:
              if nuke:
                  ids = await self.list_all_event_ids()
              else:
                  ids = await self.list_dir3_event_ids()
              if dry_run or not ids:
                  return GCalClearReport(deleted=len(ids), dry_run=dry_run)
              calendar_id = self.settings.calendar_id
              deleted = 0
              async with self._client_factory(self.settings, self.timeout) as (google, calendar):
                  for chunk in _chunks(ids, BATCH_SIZE):
                      pairs = [
                          (
                              event_id,
                              calendar.events.delete(calendarId=calendar_id, eventId=event_id),
                          )
                          for event_id in chunk
                      ]
                      # ok + gone (404/410, schon weg) zählen als erledigt
                      deleted += len(await _send_requests(google, pairs, timeout=self.timeout))
              return GCalClearReport(deleted=deleted, dry_run=False)
      
      
      def run_sync(syncer: GoogleCalendarSyncer, plan, *, timezone_name: str, dry_run: bool = False):
          """Sync-Wrapper für den synchronen CLI-Pfad."""
          return asyncio.run(syncer.sync(plan, timezone_name=timezone_name, dry_run=dry_run))
      
      
      def run_clear(syncer: GoogleCalendarSyncer, *, dry_run: bool = False, nuke: bool = False):
          """Clear-Wrapper für den synchronen CLI-Pfad."""
          return asyncio.run(syncer.clear(dry_run=dry_run, nuke=nuke))
      
      
      def _aware(dt, tz):
          return dt.astimezone(tz) if dt.tzinfo is not None else dt.replace(tzinfo=tz)
```

```
"""Studienwoche (TU Berlin): Vorlesungen/Tutorien fest, Gebete passend dazu.

Gebete: Wudu 3 min vor dem Gebet, danach 2 min pro Rakah. Voll (nicht
kritisch) nach Hanafi: Fajr 4, Dhuhr 10, Asr 8, Maghrib 5, Isha 13 Rakats
(Sunnah + Fardh + Witr, ohne Nafl). In kritischen Zeiten nur Fardh:
2/4/4/3/4. Zur Moschee kommen 10 min Weg; passt das nicht, wird allein
gebetet. Unter 30 min verfuegbarem Fenster gibt es immer keine Moschee.

Vorlesungen: Der offizielle 2-h-Block wird als 1 h 45 angezeigt, die letzten
15 min bleiben frei. Die ersten 15 min duerfen fuer Gebete genutzt werden,
wenn das Gebet (inkl. Wudu/Weg) dort hineinpasst. Wuerde ein Gebet sonst in
den letzten 30 min vor der naechsten Grenze starten, wird die Vorlesung an
dieser Stelle unterbrochen, das Gebet dort platziert und mit
"!! bricht ... ab, anders nicht möglich" markiert. Asr wird in den letzten
45 min vor Maghrib nur als Fardh gebetet und nennt zusaetzlich "Kerahat".

Freitag: Dhuhr heisst Jumuah und dauert 60 min. Die Zeit ist 12:30 in der
Winterzeit (CET) und 13:30 in der Sommerzeit (CEST); davor liegt die Fahrt
zur Moschee (aktuell 45 min, Route im Event-Titel).

Sonntag: 18:00-22:00 Netzwerken, davor derselbe Weg wie bei Jumuah; beide
Events werden mit going() gekoppelt. Isha steht fest um 18:30, sofern der
Adhan nicht spaeter liegt; sonst bleibt es beim Adhan. Netzwerken wird bei
Isha unterbrochen und nach dem Gebet fortgesetzt.

Farben: Gebete/Jumuah Basilikum; AnalinA, ROBS, IaD und GldP haben je eine
eigene Farbe; Weg ist Graphit, Netzwerken Mandarin.

Gebetszeiten: Diyanet (method 13, Shafi-Asr), Standort gepinnt (Berlin).

    dir3 gebetsplan.py --until 7 --compile   # nur drucken
    dir3 gebetsplan.py --until 7             # in Google Calendar schreiben
"""

from dataclasses import replace
from datetime import datetime, time, timedelta

from dir3 import GoogleCalendar, day, task, week
from dir3.color import PALETTE, PRAYER_NAMES, name_slot, normalize_event_name

# Diyanet (method 13), Shafi-Asr: wie die Gebetszeiten-App
prayer = {"method": 13, "school": 0, "method_auto": False}

# Standort fest gepinnt (Berlin), damit die Zeiten nicht mit der IP-Geolocation driften
location = (52.5323, 13.3846, "Europe/Berlin")

# Farben: alle Gebete/Jumuah Basilikum; jede Vorlesungsmodul-Familie eine
# eigene Farbe; Weg und Netzwerken eigene Farben. Andere Events nie Basilikum.
BASIL_SLOT = PALETTE.index("10")
PEACOCK_SLOT = PALETTE.index("7")
TOMATO_SLOT = PALETTE.index("11")
BLUEBERRY_SLOT = PALETTE.index("9")
GRAPE_SLOT = PALETTE.index("3")
TANGERINE_SLOT = PALETTE.index("6")
GRAPHITE_SLOT = PALETTE.index("8")
LAVENDER_SLOT = PALETTE.index("1")


class GebetsplanColorPolicy:
    """Gebete/Jumuah Basilikum, Modulgruppen und Wege feste Farben."""

    def color_for(self, name, index):
        normalized = normalize_event_name(name)
        head = normalized.split(" ", 1)[0]
        if head in PRAYER_NAMES:
            return BASIL_SLOT
        if normalized.startswith("weg"):
            return GRAPHITE_SLOT
        if "analina" in normalized:
            return PEACOCK_SLOT
        if "robs" in normalized:
            return TOMATO_SLOT
        if "iad" in normalized:
            return BLUEBERRY_SLOT
        if "gldp" in normalized:
            return GRAPE_SLOT
        if "netzwerken" in normalized:
            return TANGERINE_SLOT
        slot = name_slot(normalized)
        return LAVENDER_SLOT if slot == BASIL_SLOT else slot


color_policy = GebetsplanColorPolicy()

WUDU = 3  # Minuten Wudu vor dem Azan
MIN_PER_RAKAT = 2  # Minuten pro Rakah
# Hanafi: Sunnah + Fardh (+ Witr bei Isha), ohne Nafl.
FULL_RAKATS = {"Fajr": 4, "Dhuhr": 10, "Asr": 8, "Maghrib": 5, "Isha": 13}
# Kritisch: nur die Fardh-Rakats.
FARDH_RAKATS = {"Fajr": 2, "Dhuhr": 4, "Asr": 4, "Maghrib": 3, "Isha": 4}
MOSQUE_TRAVEL = 10  # Minuten zur Moschee (einfacher Weg)
MOSQUE_WINDOW = 30  # unter 30 min Fenster: allein beten, keine Moschee
MISS_BUFFER = 30  # Restpuffer, unter dem ein volles Gebet kritisch ist
START_BUFFER = 30  # kein Gebet startet in den letzten 30 min vor der Grenze
KERAHAT_BUFFER = 45  # Asr in den letzten 45 min vor Maghrib = Kerahat
# Maghrib: nach der 16-18-Vorlesung bleiben oft <30 min bis Isha -> 20 reichen
BUFFER_OVERRIDES = {"Maghrib": 20}

ORDER = ("Fajr", "Dhuhr", "Asr", "Maghrib", "Isha")
AZAN = {"Fajr": "fajr", "Dhuhr": "dhuhr", "Asr": "asr", "Maghrib": "maghrib", "Isha": "isha"}
```

```
      class PlanError(ValueError):
          """A plan/definition error: wrong day, missing anchor, overflow, ..."""
      
      
      #: A predicate used in ``unless``: (ctx) -> True means "skip today".
      Unless = Callable[[Any], bool]
      
      
      @dataclass(slots=True)
      class Task:
          name: str
          start: Anchor | time | None = None
          until: Anchor | time | None = None
          duration: timedelta | None = None
          space: timedelta | None = None
          unless: tuple[Unless, ...] = ()
          flex: bool = True
          overlap: bool = False
      
          @property
          def anchored(self) -> bool:
              """True when the task pins itself via start/until (not merely chained)."""
              return self.start is not None or self.until is not None
      
          def describe(self) -> str:
              bits = [self.name]
              if self.start is not None:
                  bits.append(f"start={self.start!r}")
              if self.until is not None:
                  bits.append(f"until={self.until!r}")
              if self.duration is not None:
                  bits.append(f"{self.duration!s}")
              return " ".join(bits)
      
      
      def task(
          name: str,
          *,
          start: Anchor | time | None = None,
          until: Anchor | time | None = None,
          duration: timedelta | str | None = None,
          space: timedelta | str | None = None,
          unless: Unless | tuple[Unless, ...] | None = None,
          flex: bool = True,
          overlap: bool = False,
      ) -> Task:
          """Declare one task inside a day.
      
          * ``start``  - an anchor (or plain time) that starts the task;
          * ``until``  - an anchor (or time) that ends it (wraps across midnight);
          * ``duration`` - how long it lasts when no ``until`` is given;
          * ``space``  - a gap before the task (used when chaining);
          * ``unless`` - a predicate or tuple of predicates skipping the task for a day;
          * ``flex``   - whether the compiler may shrink this task to absorb overflow;
          * ``overlap`` - allow this pinned task to overlap earlier pinned blocks.
          """
          if not name.strip():
              raise PlanError("task() needs a name")
      
          duration_td = (
              duration
              if isinstance(duration, timedelta) or duration is None
              else _as_duration(duration)
          )
          space_td = (
              space if isinstance(space, timedelta) or space is None else _as_duration(space)
          )
      
          predicates: tuple[Unless, ...] = ()
          if unless is not None:
              predicates = unless if isinstance(unless, tuple) else (unless,)
      
          if until is None and duration_td is None and not flex:
              raise PlanError(f"task '{name}' needs an until anchor, a duration, or flex=True")
      
          return Task(
              name=name.strip(),
              start=start,
              until=until,
              duration=duration_td,
              space=space_td,
              unless=predicates,
              flex=flex,
              overlap=overlap,
          )
      
      
      def _as_duration(value: str) -> timedelta:
          from .timeutils import parse_duration
      
          return parse_duration(value)
      
      
      @dataclass(slots=True)
      class Day:
          name: str
          tasks: list[Task] = field(default_factory=list)
          start: Anchor | time | None = None
      
          @classmethod
          def from_factory(cls, func: DayFactory) -> Day:
              return cls(name=func.name, start=getattr(func, "start", None))
      
      
      class DayFactory:
          """Wraps a user day function ``(ctx) -> list[Task] | Day``."""
      
          def __init__(
              self,
              func: Callable[..., object],
              *,
              name: str | None = None,
              start: Anchor | time | None = None,
          ) -> None:
              self.func = func
              self.name = name or getattr(func, "__name__", "day") or "day"
              self.start = start
              self.__name__ = self.name  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
              self.__qualname__ = self.name  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
      
          def __call__(self, ctx: Any) -> object:
              return self.func(ctx)
      
      
      def day(
          arg: Any = None,
          *tasks: Task,
          name: str | None = None,
          start: Anchor | time | None = None,
      ):
          """Build a ``Day``, or decorate a function as a day factory.
      
          Builder::
      
              day("Weekday", task(...), task(...), start=morning)
      
          Decorator (returns a :class:`DayFactory`). The day's ``start`` anchor can
          be given in the decorator itself instead of pinning the first task::
      
              @day
              def workday(ctx):
                  return [task(...), ...]
      
              @day(name="Mein Tag", start=time(9, 0))
              def strukturtag(ctx):
                  return [task(...), ...]  # chains on from 09:00
          """
          if arg is None and not tasks:
              # supports ``@day(name="Titel")`` and ``@day(start=...)`` decorator forms
              def decorate(factory: Callable[..., object]) -> DayFactory:
                  return DayFactory(
                      factory,
                      name=name or getattr(factory, "__name__", None) or "day",
                      start=start,
                  )
      
              return decorate
          if callable(arg) and not tasks:
              factory = arg
              return DayFactory(
                  factory,
                  name=name or getattr(factory, "__name__", None) or "day",
                  start=start,
              )
          if isinstance(arg, str):
              return Day(name=arg, tasks=list(tasks), start=start)
          raise PlanError("day() expects a name + tasks, or a single callable to decorate")
      
      
      def week(**days: Any) -> Week:
          """A week: one day factory per weekday (``mon`` ... ``sun``)."""
          normalized: dict[str, Any] = {}
          for key, value in days.items():
              key_lower = key.strip().lower()
              if key_lower not in WEEKDAY_KEYS:
                  raise PlanError(f"Unknown weekday {key!r} (use one of {', '.join(WEEKDAY_NAMES)})")
              normalized[key_lower] = value
          return Week(days=normalized)
      
      
      @dataclass(slots=True)
      class Week:
          days: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)  # mon..sun -> DayFactory | Day | list
      
          def get(self, weekday_index: int) -> Any | None:
              return self.days.get(WEEKDAY_NAMES[weekday_index])

      class Month:
          """A repeating unit of weeks (the pattern for one month)."""
      
          weeks: list[Week]
      
          def week_for(self, index_in_unit: int) -> Week | None:
              if not self.weeks:
                  return None
              return self.weeks[index_in_unit % len(self.weeks)]
      
      
      def month(*weeks: Week) -> Month:
          """Bundle weeks into one repeating month pattern."""
          return Month(weeks=list(weeks))
      
      
      class CalendarPattern:
          """A plan as a single function: ``(date) -> day_factory | None``.
      
          ``None`` means a free day.  This is the ultimate escape hatch - the whole
          year can be *one* function that decides, per calendar date, what kind of
          day to run.
          """
      
          def __init__(self, func: Callable[[Any], Any | None]) -> None:
              self.func = func
              self.__name__ = getattr(func, "__name__", "calendar")  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
      
          def __call__(self, calendar_date: Any) -> Any | None:
              return self.func(calendar_date)
      
      
      def calendar(_func: Callable[[Any], Any | None] | None = None) -> Any:
          """Decorate a ``(date) -> day_factory | None`` function as a whole-plan pattern.
      
          Use it to program a whole semester/year/life as one function::
      
              @calendar
              def lebensjahr(today):
                  if is_ramadan(today):
                      return ramadan_day
                  if today.weekday() == 5:
                      return weekend_day
                  return work_day
          """
          if _func is None:
              raise PlanError("calendar() only works as a decorator: @calendar")
          return CalendarPattern(_func)
      
      
      #: Convenient end-of-day anchor for "until next day start" tasks.
      next_day_start = midnight
```

```
      from datetime import timedelta
      
      from dir3 import task
      
      RAKAH_DUR = 2
      WUDU_DUR = 5
      BUF = 5
      
      
      def rakat(miqdar):
          return timedelta(minutes=miqdar * RAKAH_DUR + BUF)
      
      
      def _wudu():
          return timedelta(minutes=WUDU_DUR)
      
      
      def _prayer(name, anchor, rakats):
          return task(name, start=anchor - _wudu(), duration=_wudu() + rakat(rakats))
      
      
      prayers = {
          "fajr":    lambda ctx: _prayer("Fajr", ctx.prayer.sunrise-timedelta(WUDU_DUR+20), 4),
          "dhuhr":   lambda ctx: _prayer("Dhuhr", ctx.prayer.dhuhr, 10),
          "asr":     lambda ctx: _prayer("Asr", ctx.prayer.asr, 8),
          "maghrib": lambda ctx: _prayer("Maghrib", ctx.prayer.maghrib, 5),
```

```
      """Anchors - the heart of dir3.
      
      Anything that can pin a moment in the day is an :class:`Anchor`.  You may use
      the built-ins (``prayer.*``, ``sun.*``, ``midnight``, ...) or declare *your own*
      anchor simply by writing a function and decorating it::
      
          @anchor
          def work_end(ctx):
              return ctx.resolve(business.end) - OTHER_OFFSET ...
      
      An anchor resolves to ``datetime.time`` for a given plan day - or to ``None``
      if it has no meaning on that day (the scheduler then falls back to a ``duration``
      or leaves the event flexible).
      
      Anchors form a tiny algebra: ``work_end - timedelta(hours=1)`` returns a
      derived anchor, and ``time + time`` is deliberately impossible.
      """
      from __future__ import annotations
      
      from collections.abc import Callable
      from dataclasses import dataclass
      from datetime import time, timedelta
      from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any
      
      if TYPE_CHECKING:  # pragma: no cover - typing only
          from .context import DayContext
      
      #: An anchor resolves to a time for a given day, or None if inactive.
      AnchorResolver = Callable[["DayContext"], time | None]
      
      
      def _plain_time(value: Any) -> time | None:
          """Coerce ``time`` values; everything else is left to the caller."""
          return value if isinstance(value, time) else None
      
      
      class Anchor:
          """Base class for every time anchor."""
      
          __slots__ = ("name",)
      
          def __init__(self, name: str | None = None) -> None:
              self.name = name
      
          def resolve(self, ctx: DayContext) -> time | None:  # pragma: no cover - abstract
              raise NotImplementedError
      
          def describe(self) -> str:
              return self.name or type(self).__name__
      
          # --- algebra ---------------------------------------------------------
          def __add__(self, other: object) -> Anchor:
              if isinstance(other, timedelta):
                  return DerivedAnchor(self, other)
              return NotImplemented
      
          def __radd__(self, other: object) -> Anchor:
              if isinstance(other, timedelta):
                  return DerivedAnchor(self, other)
              return NotImplemented
      
          def __sub__(self, other: object) -> Anchor:
              if isinstance(other, timedelta):
                  return DerivedAnchor(self, -other)
              return NotImplemented
      
          def __rsub__(self, other: object) -> Anchor:
              # timedelta - anchor has no useful meaning; keep it impossible.
              return NotImplemented
      
          def __repr__(self) -> str:  # pragma: no cover - debugging aid
              return f"{type(self).__name__}({self.describe()!r})"
      
      
      class FunctionAnchor(Anchor):
          """An anchor backed by a plain user function ``(ctx) -> time | None``."""
      
          __slots__ = ("func",)
      
          def __init__(self, func: AnchorResolver, *, name: str | None = None) -> None:
              super().__init__(name=name or getattr(func, "__name__", None) or "anchor")
              self.func = func
      
          def resolve(self, ctx: DayContext) -> time | None:
              result = self.func(ctx)
              if result is None or isinstance(result, time):
                  return result
              raise TypeError(
                  f"Anchor {self.describe()!r} returned {type(result).__name__}, expected time or None"
              )
      
      
      class FixedAnchor(Anchor):
          """A constant point in time, e.g. ``midnight`` for the plan day's end."""
      
          __slots__ = ("_time",)
      
          def __init__(self, moment: time, *, name: str | None = None) -> None:
              super().__init__(name=name)
              self._time = moment
      
          def resolve(self, ctx: DayContext) -> time | None:
              return self._time
      
      
      class NamedAnchor(Anchor):
          """An anchor resolved through the day context's services (e.g. ``prayer.fajr``).
      
          The resolver receives the context so the value is looked up once per day and
          kept deterministic through the context cache.
          """
      
          __slots__ = ("resolver",)
      
          def __init__(self, name: str, resolver: AnchorResolver) -> None:
              super().__init__(name=name)
              self.resolver = resolver
      
          def resolve(self, ctx: DayContext) -> time | None:
              return self.resolver(ctx)
      
      
      @dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
      class DerivedAnchor(Anchor):
          """``base + delta`` - a shifted anchor, wrapped modulo 24h."""
      
          base: Anchor
          delta: timedelta
      
          def __post_init__(self) -> None:
              object.__setattr__(self, "name", f"{self.base.describe()} {self._sign()}")
      
          def _sign(self) -> str:
              total = int(self.delta.total_seconds())
              if total >= 0:
                  return f"+{self.delta!s}"
              return str(self.delta)
      
          def resolve(self, ctx: DayContext) -> time | None:
              base_value = ctx.resolve(self.base)
              if base_value is None:
                  return None
              from .timeutils import add_time
      
              return add_time(base_value, self.delta)
      
          def describe(self) -> str:
              return f"{self.base.describe()} {self._sign()}"
      
      
      class NextEventAnchor(Anchor):
          """``until=next_event``: the start of the next concrete event.
      
          Resolves through the day context's look-ahead handle to the start time of
          the first event of the next *active* calendar day (free days are skipped).
          Returns ``None`` when no successor exists - the task then falls back to a
          duration or stays open until the day's end.
          """
      
          __slots__ = ()
      
          def resolve(self, ctx: DayContext) -> time | None:
              handle = getattr(ctx, "_next_event_handle", None)
              if handle is None:
                  return None
              return handle.next_event_start()
      
      
      # --- registry --------------------------------------------------------------
      
      _NAMED: dict[str, Anchor] = {}
      
      
      def register(anchor_value: Anchor, name: str | None = None) -> Anchor:
          if name is not None:
              anchor_value.name = name
          if anchor_value.name:
              _NAMED[anchor_value.name] = anchor_value
          return anchor_value
      
      
      def named_anchor(name: str) -> Anchor | None:
          return _NAMED.get(name)
      
      
      def all_anchors() -> dict[str, Anchor]:
          return dict(_NAMED)
      
      
      def anchor(func: AnchorResolver | Anchor | None = None, *, name: str | None = None):
          """Declare a function as a reusable time anchor.
      
          Usable as a bare decorator or with a name override::
      
              @anchor
              def work_end(ctx): ...
      
              @anchor(name="curfew")
              def home_latest(ctx): ...
          """
          if func is None:
              return lambda f: anchor(f, name=name)
      
          if isinstance(func, Anchor):
              return register(func, name=name)
      
          if not callable(func):
              raise TypeError("anchor() expects a callable taking (ctx) -> time | None")
      
          wrapped = FunctionAnchor(func, name=name or getattr(func, "__name__", None) or "anchor")
          return register(wrapped)
      
      
      # --- builtin constant anchors ----------------------------------------------
      
      #: End of the plan day: resolves to 00:00, the compiler interprets an
      #: `until` at or before the start as wrapping to the next calendar day.
      midnight = register(FixedAnchor(time(hour=0, minute=0), name="midnight"), "midnight")
      
      #: ``until=next_event`` - the first event of the next active calendar day.
      next_event = register(NextEventAnchor(name="next_event"), "next_event")

      """The planner engine: expands a month/week/day pattern into concrete days.
      
      The design goal is *not too strict*: a day is scheduled softly.
      
      * anchored tasks (``start``/``until``) pin moments in the day;
      * chained tasks flow after the previous one and may be shifted naturally;
      * flexible tasks can be shrunk when the day overflows;
      * leftover time is reported as *TO PLAN* slack instead of being force-filled.
      """
      from __future__ import annotations
      
      from dataclasses import dataclass, field
      from datetime import date, datetime, time, timedelta
      from typing import Any
      
      from .anchor import DerivedAnchor, NextEventAnchor, next_event
      from .config import Dir3Config
      from .context import DayContext
      from .core import (
          WEEKDAY_NAMES,
          CalendarPattern,
          Day,
          DayFactory,
          Month,
          PlanError,
          Task,
          Week,
      )
      from .services import Services
      from .timeutils import combine, format_time
      
      ZERO = timedelta(0)
      _DAY = timedelta(days=1)
      #: pinned starts before this hour of day are candidate "post-midnight" moments
      _DAWN_LIMIT = time(hour=4, minute=30)
      
      
      @dataclass(slots=True)
      class PlannedEvent:
          name: str
          start: datetime | None
          end: datetime | None
          skipped: bool = False
          open_: bool = False
          trimmed: timedelta = ZERO
          flexible: bool = True
          anchored: bool = False
          #: the event intentionally runs into the next calendar day
          #: (``until=next_event``, e.g. sleep until tomorrow's first event)
          carry: bool = False
      
          @property
          def active(self) -> bool:
              return not self.skipped and self.start is not None and self.end is not None
      
      
      @dataclass(slots=True)
      class PlanDay:
          date: date
          name: str
          events: list[PlannedEvent] = field(default_factory=list)
          slack: timedelta = ZERO
          overflow: timedelta = ZERO
          active: bool = True
      
          @property
          def skipped_count(self) -> int:
              return sum(1 for ev in self.events if ev.skipped)
      
          @property
          def open_count(self) -> int:
              return sum(1 for ev in self.events if ev.open_ and not ev.skipped)
      
          @property
          def trimmed_total(self) -> timedelta:
              return sum((ev.trimmed for ev in self.events), ZERO)
      
      
      @dataclass(slots=True)
      class Plan:
          title: str
          start: date
          days: list[PlanDay] = field(default_factory=list)
      
          def summary(self) -> dict[str, object]:
              total_slack = sum((day.slack for day in self.days), ZERO)
              total_over = sum((day.overflow for day in self.days), ZERO)
              planned_days = [d for d in self.days if d.active]
              return {
                  "days": len(self.days),
                  "planned_days": len(planned_days),
                  "total_slack": total_slack,
                  "total_overflow": total_over,
                  "trimmed": sum(len([ev for ev in d.events if ev.trimmed > ZERO]) for d in planned_days),
              }
      
      
      def compile_pattern(
          pattern: Month | Week | DayFactory | Any,
          *,
          until: timedelta | int | None = None,
          days: int | None = None,
          start_date: date | None = None,
          title: str | None = None,
          overrides: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
          services: Services | None = None,
          config: Dir3Config | None = None,
      ) -> Plan:
          """Compile a pattern into a concrete plan of ``days``.
      
          * ``pattern`` - a :class:`Month`, :class:`Week`, day factory or day callable;
          * ``until`` / ``days`` - horizon (``until=timedelta(days=360)``);
          * ``overrides`` - ``{"YYYY-MM-DD": day_factory}`}` - per-date exceptions;
          * ``services``/``config`` - optional, for tests / custom wiring.
          """
          total_days = _resolve_horizon(until, days)
          if total_days <= 0:
              raise PlanError("compilation horizon must be positive")
          services = services or Services(config=config)
          start = start_date or _plan_today(services)
      
          unit = _normalize_unit(pattern)
          day_overrides = dict(overrides or {})
      
          plan = Plan(title=title or "dir3 Plan", start=start)
          plan.days = [None] * total_days
          # Compile from the last day backwards: each day learns its successor, so
          # ``until=next_event`` can reach across midnight into the next active day.
          for index in range(total_days - 1, -1, -1):
              calendar = start + timedelta(days=index)
              day_def = _day_for(calendar, index, unit, day_overrides)
              if day_def is None:
                  plan.days[index] = PlanDay(date=calendar, name="———", active=False)
                  continue
              ctx = DayContext(plan_date=calendar, services=services)
              ctx._next_event_handle = _Lookahead(plan, index)
              day_model = _invoke_day(day_def, ctx)
              plan.days[index] = _compile_day(day_model, ctx)
              ctx._resolve_cache.clear()
          return plan
      
      
      def _plan_today(services: Services | None) -> date:
          """Today in the *plan's* timezone, not the machine's (portable planning).
      
          A developer whose machine dwells in another zone (server, CI, travel)
          still gets the correct day start for the planned location.  Falls back to
          the machine date when no location/zone can be resolved.
          """
          tz = None
          if services is not None:
              try:
                  tz = services.location.tzinfo
              except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - no location resolvable
                  tz = None
          try:
              now = datetime.now(tz) if tz is not None else datetime.now()
          except (ValueError, TypeError):  # pragma: no cover - defensive
              return date.today()
          return now.date()
      
      
      def _resolve_horizon(until: timedelta | int | None, days: int | None) -> int:
          if days is not None:
              return int(days)
          if until is None:
              return 30
          if isinstance(until, timedelta):
              return max(1, int(until.total_seconds() // 86400))
          return int(until)
      
      
      class _Lookahead:
          """Lets a day read its successor while being compiled.
      
          ``until=next_event`` resolves to the start of the first concrete event of
          the next *active* calendar day (free days are skipped), or ``None`` when
          the horizon ends.
          """
      
          def __init__(self, plan: Plan, index: int) -> None:
              self._plan = plan
              self._index = index
      
          def next_event_moment(self) -> datetime | None:
              """The absolute start of the first concrete event of the next active
              day, or ``None`` when the horizon ends."""
              for pday in self._plan.days[self._index + 1 :]:
                  if pday is None or not pday.active:
                      continue
                  for event in pday.events:
                      if event.active and event.start is not None:
                          return event.start
                  return None
              return None
      
          def next_event_start(self) -> time | None:
              moment = self.next_event_moment()
              return moment.time() if moment is not None else None
      
      
      def _next_event_based(until: object) -> bool:
          """True when ``until`` is ``next_event`` or a derived shift of it."""
          if until is next_event:
              return True
          return isinstance(until, DerivedAnchor) and isinstance(until.base, NextEventAnchor)
      
      
      def _normalize_unit(pattern: Any) -> list[Week] | CalendarPattern:
          if isinstance(pattern, CalendarPattern):
              return pattern
          if isinstance(pattern, Month):
              if not pattern.weeks:
                  raise PlanError("month() given no weeks")
              return list(pattern.weeks)
          if isinstance(pattern, Week):
              return [pattern]
          # a bare day factory / callable: repeat it on every weekday of the week
          if isinstance(pattern, (Day, DayFactory)) or callable(pattern):
              return [Week(days={name: pattern for name in WEEKDAY_NAMES})]
          raise PlanError(f"Cannot compile pattern {pattern!r}")
      
      
      def _day_for(
          calendar: date, index: int, unit: Any, overrides: dict[str, Any]
      ):
          iso = calendar.isoformat()
          if iso in overrides:
              return overrides[iso]
          if isinstance(unit, CalendarPattern):
              return unit(calendar)
          week_index = (index // 7) % len(unit)
          week = unit[week_index]
          return week.get(calendar.weekday())
      
      
      def _invoke_day(day_def: Any, ctx: DayContext) -> Day:
          result = day_def(ctx) if callable(day_def) else day_def
          if isinstance(result, Day):
              return result
          if isinstance(result, (list, tuple)):
              tasks = list(result)
              for item in tasks:
                  if not isinstance(item, Task):
                      raise PlanError(f"Day returned non-task element {item!r}")
              base_name = getattr(day_def, "name", None) or type(day_def).__name__
              return Day(
                  name=str(base_name),
                  tasks=tasks,
                  start=getattr(day_def, "start", None),
              )
          if isinstance(day_def, Day):
              return day_def
          raise PlanError(f"Cannot use {day_def!r} as a day definition")
      
      
      def _compile_day(day: Day, ctx: DayContext) -> PlanDay:
          cursor: datetime | None = None
          end_of_day = combine(ctx.plan_date + _DAY, time(hour=0, minute=0))
          events: list[PlannedEvent] = []
          anchored_end: datetime | None = None
      
          for item in day.tasks:
              if item.unless and any(pred(ctx) for pred in item.unless):
                  events.append(
                      PlannedEvent(name=item.name, start=None, end=None, skipped=True)
                  )
                  continue
      
              start_dt = _resolve_start(item, day, ctx, cursor)
              if start_dt is None and cursor is None:
                  raise PlanError(
                      f"'{day.name}': task '{item.name}' (or the day) needs a start anchor"
                  )
              if start_dt is None:
                  start_dt = cursor
                  if item.space:
                      start_dt += item.space
      
              anchored = item.anchored
              if anchored and anchored_end is not None and start_dt < anchored_end:
                  # A pinned start well before an earlier pinned end is a
                  # post-midnight moment (Berlin nights in June, Tahajjud, night
                  # shift): roll it into the next calendar day instead of crashing.
                  gap = anchored_end - start_dt
                  spans_a_full_block = gap >= timedelta(hours=20)
                  deep_night = start_dt.time() < _DAWN_LIMIT and gap >= timedelta(hours=12)
                  if spans_a_full_block or deep_night:
                      start_dt += _DAY
                  elif not item.overlap:
                      raise PlanError(
                          f"'{day.name}': '{item.name}' at {format_time(start_dt.time())} "
                          f"overlaps a pinned block that ends at {format_time(anchored_end.time())}"
                      )
      
              end_dt, open_task, via_next_event = _resolve_end(item, ctx, start_dt, end_of_day)
      
              carry = via_next_event and end_dt is not None and end_dt.date() > ctx.plan_date
      
              if anchored and end_dt is not None and (anchored_end is None or end_dt > anchored_end):
                  anchored_end = end_dt  # for tasks without duration, use their span
      
              event = PlannedEvent(
                  name=item.name,
                  start=start_dt,
                  end=end_dt,
                  open_=open_task,
                  flexible=item.flex,
                  anchored=anchored,
                  carry=carry,
              )
              events.append(event)
              if end_dt is not None:
                  cursor = end_dt
      
          return _balance(PlanDay(date=ctx.plan_date, name=day.name, events=events), cursor, end_of_day)
      
      
      def _resolve_start(
          item: Task, day: Day, ctx: DayContext, cursor: datetime | None
      ) -> datetime | None:
          if item.start is not None:
              value = ctx.resolve(item.start)
              if value is not None:
                  return combine(ctx.plan_date, value)
          # the day may provide its own start (``@day(start=...)``) as a fallback
          # pinned before any task chains
          if cursor is None and day.start is not None:
              value = ctx.resolve(day.start)
              if value is not None:
                  return combine(ctx.plan_date, value)
          return None
      
      
      def _resolve_end(
          item: Task,
          ctx: DayContext,
          start_dt: datetime,
          end_of_day: datetime,
      ) -> tuple[datetime | None, bool, bool]:
          """Resolve the task's end. Returns ``(end, open_, from_next_event)``.
      
          ``from_next_event`` is True when the end came from the ``until=next_event``
          look-ahead (absolute date, so free days in between are honored).
          """
          if _next_event_based(item.until):
              handle = getattr(ctx, "_next_event_handle", None)
              if handle is not None:
                  target = handle.next_event_moment()
                  if target is not None:
                      delta = (
                          item.until.delta  # type: ignore[union-attr]
                          if isinstance(item.until, DerivedAnchor)
                          else ZERO
                      )
                      end_dt = target + delta
                      if item.duration is not None and end_dt - start_dt < item.duration:
                          raise PlanError(
                              f"'{item.name}': duration {item.duration!s} does not fit "
                              "before its 'next_event'"
                          )
                      return end_dt, False, True
          if item.until is not None:
              value = ctx.resolve(item.until)
              if value is not None:
                  end_dt = combine(ctx.plan_date, value)
                  if end_dt <= start_dt:
                      end_dt += _DAY
                  if item.duration is not None and end_dt - start_dt < item.duration:
                      raise PlanError(
                          f"'{item.name}': duration {item.duration!s} does not fit before its 'until'"
                      )
                  return end_dt, False, False
          if item.duration is not None:
              return start_dt + item.duration, False, False
          if item.flex:
              return end_of_day, True, False
          raise PlanError(f"Task '{item.name}' has neither until, duration nor flex=True")
      
      
      def _balance(pday: PlanDay, cursor: datetime | None, end_of_day: datetime) -> PlanDay:
          """Compensate overflow by shrinking flexible tasks; report slack otherwise."""
          if cursor is None:
              pday.active = False
              return pday
          if cursor > end_of_day:
              if pday.events and pday.events[-1].carry:
                  # a carried event (e.g. sleep ``until=next_event``) runs into the
                  # next morning on purpose - that is not overflow, and the night
                  # belongs to the plan.
                  pday.slack = ZERO
              else:
                  needed = cursor - end_of_day
                  for event in reversed(pday.events):
                      if needed <= ZERO:
                          break
                      if not event.active or event.open_ or not event.flexible or event.anchored:
                          continue
                      span = event.end - event.start
                      if span <= ZERO:
                          continue
                      trim = min(needed, span)
                      event.end -= trim
                      event.trimmed += trim
                      needed -= trim
                  pday.overflow = max(needed, ZERO)
          elif cursor < end_of_day:
              pday.slack = end_of_day - cursor
          return pday

      """Human-readable output: the compiled plan, printed softly."""
      from __future__ import annotations
      
      from datetime import timedelta
      
      from .color import DefaultIconPolicy, event_summary
      from .engine import Plan, PlanDay, PlannedEvent
      from .timeutils import format_duration, format_time
      
      #: Standard-Icon-Policy für die Render-Ausgabe
      _DEFAULT_ICON_POLICY = DefaultIconPolicy()
      
      WEEKDAY_LABELS = ("Mo", "Di", "Mi", "Do", "Fr", "Sa", "So")
      
      
      def weekday_label(plan_date) -> str:  # datetime.date
          return WEEKDAY_LABELS[plan_date.weekday()]
      
      
      def render_plan(plan: Plan) -> str:
          lines: list[str] = []
          header = f"dir3 — {plan.title}  ({plan.start.isoformat()} → +{len(plan.days)} Tage)"
          lines.append(header)
          lines.append("=" * len(header))
          for idx, day in enumerate(plan.days):
              lines.append(_render_day(idx, day))
          summary = plan.summary()
          lines.append("-" * max(len(header), 20))
          lines.append(
              f"{summary['planned_days']} geplante Tage · "
              f"TO PLAN gesamt {format_duration(summary['total_slack'])} · "
              f"trimmed {summary['trimmed']} Events"
          )
          if (summary["total_overflow"]) > timedelta(0):
              lines.append(
                  f"⚠  {format_duration(summary['total_overflow'])} passen nicht "
                  "(auch nach Kompensation) - Plan kürzen."
              )
          return "\n".join(lines)
      
      
      def _render_day(index: int, day: PlanDay) -> str:
          date_str = f"{weekday_label(day.date)} {day.date.isoformat()}"
          if not day.active:
              return f"{date_str}  [frei]"
          events = [ev for ev in day.events]
          lines = [f"{date_str}  ·  {event_summary(day.name, _DEFAULT_ICON_POLICY)}"]
          for ev in events:
              lines.append("  " + _render_event(ev))
          notes: list[str] = []
          if day.skipped_count:
              notes.append(f"{day.skipped_count} übersprungen")
          if day.trimmed_total > timedelta(0):
              notes.append(f"trimmed {format_duration(day.trimmed_total)}")
          flags = " · ".join(notes)
          slack_text = f"TO PLAN {format_duration(day.slack)}" if day.slack > timedelta(0) else "voll"
          line = f"      [{slack_text}]"
          if flags:
              line += f" | {flags}"
          if day.overflow > timedelta(0):
              line += f" | ⚠ Überlauf {format_duration(day.overflow)}"
          lines.append(line)
          return "\n".join(lines)
      
      
      def _render_event(ev: PlannedEvent) -> str:
          if ev.skipped:
              return f"⏭  {event_summary(ev.name, _DEFAULT_ICON_POLICY)}   (entfällt)"
          start_text = format_time(ev.start.time()) if ev.start else "--:--"
          end_text = format_time(ev.end.time()) if ev.end else "offen"
          body = f"{start_text} – {end_text}   {event_summary(ev.name, _DEFAULT_ICON_POLICY)}"
          if ev.open_:
              body += "   (offen)"
          if ev.carry:
              body += "   (läuft ins Folgetag)"
          if ev.trimmed > timedelta(0):
              body += f"   [gestaucht -{format_duration(ev.trimmed)}]"
          return body
```

```
      """Ein Tag, der sich an den Gebetszeiten ausrichtet - der munazzim-Fall.
      
      `ctx.prayer` liefert pro Kalendertag frische Anker (fajr, sunrise, dhuhr,
      asr, maghrib, isha); davon lassen sich mit `- timedelta(...)` abgeleitete
      Anker bauen. Alles wird pro Tag lazy aufgelöst.
      """
      from datetime import time, timedelta
      
      from dir3 import day as _day
      from dir3 import next_day_start, task, week
      
      # --- Standort (dein Ort, hier im Planfile) ----------------------------------
      # lat, lon, IANA-Zeitzone. Ohne diese Zeile bestimmt dir3 ihn per Geolocation.
      location = (40.7992, 29.4305, "Europe/Istanbul")
      
      
      @_day(name="Gebets-Tag")
      def day(ctx):
          p = ctx.prayer
          return [
              task("Read", start=time(4, 0), until=p.sunrise - timedelta(minutes=30)),
              task("Fajr", until=p.sunrise),
              task("Arabic Shi'r", duration=timedelta(minutes=51)),
              task("Breakfast", duration=timedelta(hours=1)),
              task("Read", until=p.dhuhr - timedelta(minutes=10)),
              task("Dhuhr", until=p.dhuhr + timedelta(minutes=30)),
              task("Research", space=timedelta(hours=1), until=p.asr - timedelta(minutes=10)),
              task("Asr", until=p.asr + timedelta(minutes=20)),
              task("Eat Food", duration=timedelta(hours=1, minutes=30)),
              task("Family Time", until=p.maghrib - timedelta(minutes=10)),
              task("Maghrib", until=p.maghrib + timedelta(minutes=20)),
              task("Isha", start=p.isha - timedelta(minutes=10), until=p.isha + timedelta(minutes=30)),
              task("Sleep", until=next_day_start),
          ]
      
      
      def make_plan():
          """Rufe es direkt auf: `dir3 examples/templates/pray_based_home_routine.py --until 1`."""
          return week(mon=day, tue=day, wed=day, thu=day, fri=day, sat=day, sun=day)
```

```
      """Trait-like event colors: policies, GCal rendering, provider wiring."""
      from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
      from datetime import date, timedelta
      from types import SimpleNamespace
      
      from dir3 import cli
      from dir3.color import (
          GREEN_SLOT,
          ORANGE_SLOT,
          RED_SLOT,
          YELLOW_SLOT,
          ColorPolicy,
          DictColorPolicy,
          PlainPolicy,
          PrayerColorPolicy,
          PrayerStatusColorPolicy,
          name_slot,
          normalize_event_name,
          to_gcal_color_id,
      )
      from dir3.config import Dir3Config, LocationSettings, PrayerSettings
      from dir3.core import day, task, week
      from dir3.engine import compile_pattern
      from dir3.services import Services
      from dir3.services.gcal import (
          GCalSyncReport,
          GoogleCalendar,
          GoogleCalendarSyncer,
      )
      
      ISTANBUL = LocationSettings(latitude=40.7992, longitude=29.4305, timezone="Europe/Istanbul")
      
      
      def _coding_day():
          @day
          def coding(ctx):
              return [
                  task("Fajr", start=ctx.prayer.fajr, until=ctx.prayer.sunrise),
                  task("Coding", duration=timedelta(hours=2)),
                  task("Reading", duration=timedelta(hours=1)),
              ]
      
          return coding
      
      
      def _one_day_plan():
          config = Dir3Config(location=ISTANBUL, prayer=PrayerSettings(provider="offline"))
          coding = _coding_day()
          return compile_pattern(
              week(mon=coding, tue=coding, wed=coding, thu=coding, fri=coding, sat=coding, sun=coding),
              days=1,
              start_date=date(2026, 9, 14),
              services=Services(config=config),
          )
      
      
      def _syncer(**kwargs):
          settings = GoogleCalendar(client_id="c", client_secret="s", refresh_token="r")
          return GoogleCalendarSyncer(settings, **kwargs)
      
      
      def test_prayers_always_yellow():
          from dir3.color import YELLOW_SLOT
      
          policy = PrayerColorPolicy()
          for name in ("Fajr", "FAJR", "  dhuhr  ", "Duhr", "Asr", "Maghrib", "Isha", "Sunrise"):
              assert policy.color_for(name, 0) == YELLOW_SLOT
              assert policy.color_for(name, 7) == YELLOW_SLOT
          assert to_gcal_color_id(YELLOW_SLOT) == "5"  # Banana
      
      
      def test_prayer_status_policy_colors_shifted_critical_and_lecture_overlap():
          policy = PrayerStatusColorPolicy()
          assert policy.color_for("Dhuhr", 0) == GREEN_SLOT
          assert policy.color_for("Asr (verschoben: Adhan 14:14 → 15:50)", 0) == YELLOW_SLOT
          assert policy.color_for("Maghrib (kritisch, noch 22 min bis Isha-Adhan)", 0) == RED_SLOT
          assert (
              policy.color_for("Asr (Kerahat, noch 42 min bis Maghrib-Adhan)", 0)
              == RED_SLOT
          )
          assert policy.color_for("Maghrib (11 min von der Vorlesung)", 0) == ORANGE_SLOT
          assert (
              policy.color_for("Jumuah (verschoben: Adhan 11:51 → 12:30)", 0)
              == YELLOW_SLOT
          )
          assert (
              policy.color_for("Maghrib (verschoben, 11 min von der Vorlesung)", 0)
              == ORANGE_SLOT
          )
          assert (
              policy.color_for(
                  "Maghrib (verschoben, kritisch, noch 20 min bis Isha-Adhan, "
                  "11 min von der Vorlesung)",
                  0,
              )
              == RED_SLOT
          )
          assert to_gcal_color_id(ORANGE_SLOT) == "6"  # Tangerine
          assert to_gcal_color_id(GREEN_SLOT) == "2"  # Sage
          assert to_gcal_color_id(RED_SLOT) == "11"  # Tomato
          assert policy.color_for("Asr Analysis", 0) == name_slot("asr analysis")
          assert policy.color_for("Coding", 0) == name_slot("coding")
      
      
      def test_name_hash_deterministic_per_name():
          from dir3.color import name_slot
      
          policy = PrayerColorPolicy()
          # sum(b"coding") = 628 -> 628 % 11 = 1, independent of position
          assert name_slot("Coding") == 1
          assert policy.color_for("Coding", 0) == 1
          assert policy.color_for("Coding", 9) == 1
          assert policy.color_for("coding", 4) == 1  # case-insensitive
          # sum(b"reading") = 730 -> 730 % 11 = 4
          assert name_slot("Reading") == 4
          assert policy.color_for("Reading", 0) == 4
      
      
      def test_plain_policy_disables_colors():
          assert PlainPolicy().color_for("Fajr", 0) is None
          assert PlainPolicy().color_for("Coding", 3) is None
      
      
      def test_to_gcal_color_id_palette_and_bounds():
          assert to_gcal_color_id(0) == "3"  # Fajr -> grape
          assert to_gcal_color_id(4) == "11"  # Maghrib -> tomato
          assert to_gcal_color_id(5) == "9"  # Isha -> blueberry
          assert to_gcal_color_id(11) is None
          assert to_gcal_color_id(-1) is None
          assert to_gcal_color_id("xx") is None
          assert to_gcal_color_id(True) is None
      
      
      def test_normalize_event_name():
          assert normalize_event_name("  Fajr ") == "fajr"
          assert normalize_event_name(None) == ""
      
      
      def test_dict_policy_overrides_and_falls_back():
          policy = DictColorPolicy({"Coding": 9, "fajr": "11"}, fallback=PrayerColorPolicy())
          assert to_gcal_color_id(policy.color_for("Coding", 0)) == "9"  # round-trip
          assert to_gcal_color_id(policy.color_for("coding", 5)) == "9"  # case-insensitive
          assert to_gcal_color_id(policy.color_for("Fajr", 0)) == "11"  # round-trip
          assert policy.color_for("Dhuhr", 0) == 2  # prayer yellow fallback
          assert policy.color_for("Reading", 4) == 4  # name-hashed fallback
      
      
      def test_dict_policy_ignores_invalid_values():
          from dir3.color import name_slot
      
          policy = DictColorPolicy({"A": 99, "B": "xx", "C": True, "D": 0})
          # invalid overrides dropped -> name-hashed fallback (a->9, b->10, c->0, d->1)
          assert policy.color_for("A", 1) == name_slot("a") == 9
          assert policy.color_for("B", 1) == name_slot("b") == 10
          assert policy.color_for("C", 1) == name_slot("c") == 0
          assert policy.color_for("D", 1) == name_slot("d") == 1
      
      
      def test_custom_trait_impl_needs_no_inheritance():
          class SleepBlue:
              def color_for(self, name, index):
                  return 9 if "sleep" in name.lower() else None
      
          assert isinstance(SleepBlue(), ColorPolicy)
          assert SleepBlue().color_for("Sleep", 0) == 9
          assert SleepBlue().color_for("Work", 0) is None
      
      
      def test_stage_applies_policy_colors():
          staged = _syncer().stage(_one_day_plan(), timezone_name="Europe/Istanbul")
          by_name = {e.summary: e for e in staged}
          assert by_name["Fajr"].body["colorId"] == "5"  # yellow
          assert by_name["Coding"].body["colorId"] == "6"  # hashed slot 1
          assert by_name["Reading"].body["colorId"] == "11"  # hashed slot 4
      
      
      def test_stage_dict_override_wins():
          syncer = _syncer(color_policy=DictColorPolicy({"Coding": 11}))
          by_name = {
              e.summary: e for e in syncer.stage(_one_day_plan(), timezone_name="Europe/Istanbul")
          }
          assert by_name["Coding"].body["colorId"] == "11"
          assert by_name["Fajr"].body["colorId"] == "5"  # yellow fallback intact
      
      
      def test_stage_plain_policy_omits_color_id():
          staged = _syncer(color_policy=PlainPolicy()).stage(
              _one_day_plan(), timezone_name="Europe/Istanbul"
          )
          assert all("colorId" not in e.body for e in staged)
      
      
      def test_config_overlay_merges_colors():
          config = Dir3Config()
          config.overlay(SimpleNamespace(colors={"Coding": 9}))
          config.overlay(SimpleNamespace(colors={"Reading": "5"}))
          assert config.colors == {"Coding": 9, "Reading": "5"}
          config.overlay(SimpleNamespace())
          assert config.colors == {"Coding": 9, "Reading": "5"}
      
      
      def test_config_overlay_accepts_color_policy():
          policy = PrayerStatusColorPolicy()
          config = Dir3Config()
          config.overlay(SimpleNamespace(color_policy=policy))
          assert config.color_policy is policy
          config.overlay(SimpleNamespace(color_policy=object()))
          assert config.color_policy is policy
      
      
      def test_cli_passes_colors_to_syncer(tmp_path, monkeypatch, capsys):
          planfile = tmp_path / "plan.py"
          planfile.write_text(
              "from datetime import time, timedelta\n"
              "from dir3 import GoogleCalendar, day, task\n"
              "from dir3.core import week\n\n"
              "location = (40.7992, 29.4305, 'Europe/Istanbul')\n"
              'gcal = GoogleCalendar(client_id="c", client_secret="s", refresh_token="r")\n'
              'colors = {"SyncTest": 9}\n\n'
              "@day\n"
              "def sample(ctx):\n"
              "    return [task('SyncTest', start=time(9, 0), duration=timedelta(minutes=30))]\n\n"
              "plan = week(mon=sample, tue=sample, wed=sample, thu=sample,\n"
              "            fri=sample, sat=sample, sun=sample)\n",
              encoding="utf-8",
          )
          recorded = {}
      
          def fake_syncer(settings, **kwargs):
              recorded.update(kwargs)
              return object()
      
          def fake_run(syncer, plan, *, timezone_name, dry_run):
              return GCalSyncReport(total=1, created=1, updated=0, dry_run=False)
      
          monkeypatch.setattr(cli, "GoogleCalendarSyncer", fake_syncer)
          monkeypatch.setattr(cli, "run_sync", fake_run)
      
          assert cli.main([str(planfile), "--offline", "--until", "1", "--sync-gcal"]) == 0
          policy = recorded.get("color_policy")
          assert isinstance(policy, DictColorPolicy)
          assert to_gcal_color_id(policy.color_for("SyncTest", 0)) == "9"
          capsys.readouterr()
      
      
      def test_cli_passes_custom_color_policy(tmp_path, monkeypatch, capsys):
          planfile = tmp_path / "plan.py"
          planfile.write_text(
              "from datetime import time, timedelta\n"

              "color_policy = PrayerStatusColorPolicy()\n\n"
              "@day\n"
              "def sample(ctx):\n"
              "    return [task('Asr (verschoben: Adhan 14:00 → 14:15)',\n"

              "plan = week(mon=sample, tue=sample, wed=sample, thu=sample,\n"

      def test_sync_bodies_carry_color_id():
          import asyncio
      
          bodies = []
      
          class _Status:
              status_code = 201
      
              def raise_for_status(self):
                  pass
      
          class _FakeEvents:
              def insert(self, **kwargs):
                  assert "body" not in kwargs, "aiogoogle takes json=, not body="
                  bodies.append(kwargs["json"])
                  return ("insert", kwargs)
      
              def update(self, **kwargs):
                  return ("update", kwargs)
      
          class _FakeCal:
              events = _FakeEvents()
      
          class _FakeAg:
              async def discover(self, *args, **kwargs):
                  return _FakeCal()
      
              async def as_user(self, *requests, **kwargs):
                  responses = [_Status() for _ in requests]
                  return responses if len(responses) > 1 else responses[0]
      
          @asynccontextmanager
          async def open_client(settings, timeout):
              yield _FakeAg(), _FakeCal()
      
          syncer = _syncer(client_factory=open_client)
          asyncio.run(syncer.sync(_one_day_plan(), timezone_name="Europe/Istanbul"))
          assert bodies and all("colorId" in body for body in bodies)
```
